For farms with good or excellent health status that are breeding eligible, calculate the total feed cost for those farms where the breed type is either Holstein or Simmental, but only if their milk yield exceeds the average milk yield of all Jersey farms with good health status, and exclude any farm whose feed cost per liter of milk (for non-zero milk production) is above 0.45 USD?

What is the difference in average feed costs between two groups: Group A consists of Holstein farms with excellent health status and milk yield above 800L, and Group B consists of non-Holstein dairy breeds (Jersey, Guernsey) with good health status and breeding eligibility, but only considering farms from Group B where their milk yield is within 50L of the median milk yield of all breeding-eligible dairy farms?

title: Livestock Breeding Performance Data
questions: Among farms with dairy breeds (Holstein and Jersey) that are in breeding programs, what is the average feed cost for those farms whose milk yield exceeds the median milk yield of all dairy farms in breeding programs, but only if their health status is either Excellent or Good?

For non-dairy breeds (Angus, Simmental, Charolais) with Fair or Good health status, calculate the total feed cost of farms that are either in breeding programs with feed costs below 370 USD OR not in breeding programs with feed costs above 380 USD, then subtract the count of Excellent health status farms among all non-dairy breeds.

What is the difference between the maximum milk yield among Holstein farms in breeding programs with Excellent health and the average feed cost of Jersey farms that are either not in breeding programs with Good health status OR in breeding programs with feed costs between 390-420 USD and Fair health status?

title: Regional Livestock Breeding Performance Data
questions: Among farms with either complete vaccination status OR production scores above 8.0 (but not both conditions simultaneously), and excluding any farms with monthly feed costs below $2000, what is the total head count for cattle and pig farms combined?

For farms that have partial vaccination status AND either head counts exceeding 80 OR production scores between 7.5-8.5 (inclusive), calculate the average monthly feed cost, but only include farms where the feed cost per head is greater than $25?

Considering only farms with complete vaccination status, if we were to redistribute livestock such that each qualifying farm type (cattle, sheep, pigs, goats) maintains exactly 3 farms, which livestock type would require the smallest total monthly feed cost adjustment from their current combined costs?

title: Agricultural Product Sales Orders
questions: Among orders where the product type is either Wheat or Soybeans but not both premium quality and from the North region, and excluding any orders with quantity less than 35 tons, what is the total revenue of orders that have a price per ton above the average price per ton of all Corn orders?

For regions that have at least one premium quality order and at least one non-premium order, calculate the weighted average quantity (weighted by price per ton) for orders where the product type is not Rice, then identify which region has the highest weighted average among those that also have total order value exceeding $50,000?

If premium quality orders received a 15% price bonus and non-premium orders with quantity above 40 tons received a 8% quantity bonus, what would be the difference in total revenue between the East and West regions for orders of Wheat, Corn, or Soybeans (excluding Rice) that have either premium quality or quantity above 35 tons?

title: Agricultural Product Sales Orders
questions: Among orders where the product type is either Wheat or Soybeans but not both in the same calculation, and the customer is premium, what is the total revenue from delivered orders minus the total revenue from cancelled orders, considering only orders with quantities above 2000 units?

For premium customers who ordered Corn or Rice, but excluding any orders with unit prices below 40.00, what is the average quantity of pending orders divided by the count of delivered orders, rounded to the nearest whole number?

If we group orders by product type, then filter for products where at least one premium customer order was cancelled AND at least one non-premium customer order was delivered, what is the sum of quantities for all pending orders within these qualifying product groups?

title: Agricultural Product Sales Orders
questions: Among orders that are either premium grade wheat with quantity above 100 tons OR non-premium soybeans with unit price above 450 USD, but excluding any cancelled orders, what is the total revenue generated by delivered orders only?

For product types where the average quantity of premium grade orders exceeds the average quantity of non-premium orders by at least 20 tons, and considering only orders with unit price between 300-400 USD, how many pending orders exist across these qualifying product types?

If we rank product types by their total delivered quantity (premium grade only), then apply a bonus multiplier of 1.2 to the revenue of the top-ranked product type and 1.1 to the second-ranked, while excluding any product type with fewer than 2 premium delivered orders, what is the adjusted total revenue difference between the top two qualifying product types?

title: Farm Machinery Operation Logs
questions: Among machines that operated on fields larger than 25 acres AND consumed more fuel per hour than the average fuel consumption rate of all Plowing operations, but excluding those requiring maintenance, what is the total field size covered by Harvesting operations only?

For machines performing either Seeding OR Fertilizing operations (but not both types appearing for the same machine ID), calculate the weighted efficiency score using the formula: (Field_Size_Acres / Fuel_Consumed_Gallons) * Hours_Operated. Then, among machines with efficiency scores above the median of this subset AND not requiring maintenance, what is the average hours operated?

If we exclude all Plowing operations that require maintenance, then among the remaining operations, identify machines where the fuel consumption per acre is below the 75th percentile of all non-Plowing operations. For these qualified machines, group by operation type and find which operation type has the highest total hours operated, but only consider operation types that appear at least 3 times in this filtered subset.

title: Farm Machinery Operation Logs
questions: Among machines that operated for more than 7 hours AND consumed less than 50 liters of fuel, but excluding those with maintenance due, what is the total field size covered by machines performing either Plowing or Seeding operations, weighted by their fuel efficiency (field size per liter consumed)?

For machines requiring maintenance that operated on fields larger than 10 hectares, calculate the average hours operated, but only include those where the fuel consumption rate (liters per hour) is below the median rate of all Harvesting operations, and exclude any machine that has the highest fuel consumption in its operation type category.

Identify machines where the operation type is NOT Fertilizing AND the field size exceeds the average field size of machines with maintenance due, then among these, find those with fuel efficiency (hectares per liter) above the 75th percentile of all machines, and calculate the total hours operated by machines that also have fuel consumption below 40 liters.

title: Farm Machinery Operation Logs
questions: Among equipment that either requires maintenance or has operated more than 10 hours (but not both conditions), and excluding any fertilizing operations, what is the total fuel consumption of plowing equipment that has worked on fields larger than 15 hectares?

For equipment that requires maintenance and has consumed more than 50 liters of fuel, but excluding those with the highest fuel efficiency (fuel per hectare) within each operation type, what is the average field size of the remaining equipment?

If we group equipment by operation type, then within each group select only those that either require maintenance or have operated less than 8 hours, what is the total hours operated by the operation type that has the second-highest average fuel consumption per hour among the filtered groups?

title: Farmer Production Input-Output Analysis
questions: Among farmers who grow either wheat or soybeans but not corn, and who are premium eligible, what is the average profit margin percentage for those whose yield exceeds the median yield of all premium-eligible farmers in their respective crop categories?

For farmers whose input costs are above the 75th percentile of their crop type and who are either not premium eligible or have yields below 20 tons, what is the total revenue difference between the highest and lowest performing farmer when premium eligible farmers receive a 15% price bonus?

What is the farmer ID of the producer who has the highest profit-to-cost ratio among those who grow crops with market prices above $300 per ton, are premium eligible, but only if we exclude farmers whose yields are in the bottom quartile of all farmers growing the same crop type?

title: Farmer Production Input-Output Analysis
questions: Among farms that either produce premium quality crops OR use drip irrigation (but not both), and have input costs above the median for their crop type, what is the average yield of those farms that also have yields exceeding 75% of farms growing the same crop?

For farms growing wheat or corn that do not use flood irrigation, if we exclude those with the lowest input cost in each crop category, what is the total yield difference between premium quality producers and non-premium producers, considering only farms whose yield-to-cost ratio exceeds the overall average?

Among rice and soybean farms that either have premium quality OR use sprinkler/drip irrigation (but farms with both premium quality AND sprinkler/drip are excluded), what is the count of farms whose input costs are within 10% of their crop type's median AND whose yields rank in the top 60% within their respective crop categories?

title: Farmer Production Input-Output Analysis
questions: Among farms that are either organic-certified wheat producers OR non-organic corn producers with drip irrigation, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, calculate the average yield-to-cost ratio (tons per $1000 input cost) for those farms whose input costs exceed the median input cost of all farms in the dataset, then identify how many such farms have yields above this calculated average ratio multiplied by their individual input costs divided by 1000?

For farms growing crops that require flood irrigation AND have input costs in the top 40% of all farms, but excluding any organic-certified rice farms, determine the total yield difference between farms with above-median yields versus below-median yields within this filtered group, then calculate what percentage this difference represents of the total yield from non-organic soybeans farms with sprinkler irrigation systems?

Identify farms where the crop type is wheat OR soybeans, the irrigation type is NOT flood, and the farm is organic-certified, then among these farms, find those whose yield per dollar of input (yield/input_cost) exceeds the average yield per dollar of all corn farms with drip irrigation, and finally determine the sum of input costs for farms in this final group that also have yields greater than the 75th percentile yield of all wheat farms in the dataset?

title: Soil Moisture Monitoring Records
questions: Among fields with active irrigation that have either wheat or soybeans (but not corn), and where the temperature is below 25°C or the soil moisture is above 50%, what is the average number of days since last rain for those fields that also have soil moisture levels that are either in the bottom 25% or top 25% of all fields in the dataset?

For fields where irrigation status is inactive and days since last rain exceed the median value across all fields, but excluding any corn fields with temperature above 30°C, what is the total soil moisture percentage when considering only those fields whose moisture levels are within 10 percentage points of the overall average moisture level?

If we group fields by crop type and consider only those groups where at least 2 fields have active irrigation and the group's average temperature is between 20-28°C, then within these qualifying groups, how many individual fields have soil moisture below 40% AND days since last rain greater than the group's median days since last rain?

title: Soil Moisture Monitoring Records
questions: Among fields with active irrigation that have either wheat or soybean crops, but excluding those with temperatures above 25°C unless their soil moisture is above 50%, what is the average yield potential score for fields that also have soil moisture levels within the optimal range of 40-55% and temperatures below the median temperature of all active irrigation fields?

For fields growing corn with inactive irrigation status, compare the total yield potential score of those with soil moisture below 35% and temperatures above 30°C against fields with soil moisture above 35% but temperatures below 30°C, then determine which group has the higher total and by how much?

Considering only fields where the irrigation status is active and the crop type is not corn, calculate the weighted average yield potential score where the weight is determined by soil moisture percentage, but only include fields that satisfy both conditions: temperature is either below 22°C or above 28°C, and yield potential score exceeds the average yield potential of all wheat fields by at least 5 points?
answers: The second group has higher total by 7 points (154 vs 147)

title: Soil Moisture Monitoring Records
questions: Among fields with active irrigation that have either high moisture (>50%) or low temperature (<25°C), but excluding those growing wheat that haven't received rain in more than 5 days, what is the average soil moisture percentage of the remaining fields?

For fields where irrigation status differs from the optimal condition (active for moisture <40% or inactive for moisture >60%), and the crop type is either corn or soybeans, how many fields have a temperature above the median temperature of all fields in the dataset?

Consider fields that meet exactly one of these criteria: (moisture >45% AND temperature <25°C) OR (days since rain <5 AND irrigation inactive). Among these fields, what is the total count of wheat and soybean fields combined, excluding any field where the temperature exceeds 30°C?

title: Rural Farm Water and Electricity Usage Data
questions: Among farms that use either drip or sprinkler irrigation (but not flood), have solar panels installed, are subsidy eligible, and generate revenue above the median revenue of all farms, what is the total water usage of those located in regions where the average electricity usage per farm exceeds 4000 KWH?

For farms growing crops that require high water usage (rice or soybeans), calculate the weighted average electricity consumption where the weight is determined by revenue rank within each region, but exclude farms that have both solar panels and drip irrigation systems, and only consider farms from regions where at least 2 farms are subsidy eligible.

What is the difference in average annual revenue between two groups: Group A consists of farms with above-average water usage that either lack solar panels or use flood irrigation (but not both conditions), while Group B includes farms with below-average electricity usage that are subsidy eligible and located in regions with exactly 4 or more farms represented?

title: Rural Farm Water and Electricity Usage Data
questions: Among farms in North and South regions that use either Drip or Sprinkler irrigation (but not Flood), calculate the average electricity usage for those with solar panels, then identify how many farms without solar panels in these same filtered regions and irrigation types have electricity usage above this calculated average?

For farms that have solar panels AND use more than 1500 m3 of water monthly, compare the total electricity consumption of Drip irrigation farms versus non-Drip irrigation farms, then determine which irrigation type (among Sprinkler and Flood only) has the higher average electricity usage within the non-Drip group?

Identify farms in East or West regions that either (have solar panels AND use Flood irrigation) OR (don't have solar panels AND use more than 1800 m3 water monthly), then calculate what percentage of these farms have electricity usage that exceeds the overall average electricity usage of all Sprinkler irrigation farms across all regions?

title: Rural Water and Electricity Usage by Village
questions: Among villages that use either Drip or Sprinkler irrigation (but not Flood), are eligible for subsidies, and have populations between 300-600, what is the average electricity usage per capita for those villages whose water usage exceeds the median water usage of all subsidy-eligible villages?

For villages with Flood irrigation that are NOT subsidy eligible, compare their total water usage against villages with Drip irrigation that ARE subsidy eligible and have above-average population (relative to all villages). Which group has higher total water usage and by how much?

If we rank all villages by their electricity-to-water usage ratio, then filter for only those villages that either have Sprinkler irrigation with subsidy eligibility OR have Drip irrigation with population above 500, what is the total population of the top 3 villages in this filtered ranking?
answers: Drip subsidy-eligible villages with above-average population have higher total water usage by 2200 KL

title: Regional Athletic Competition Results
questions: Among athletes who are bonus eligible and have a regional rank of 5 or better, what is the average score of those who train more than 40 hours per week, excluding any gymnasts who scored below 900 points?

For track athletes who are not bonus eligible OR swimmers who are bonus eligible with regional rank worse than 6, what is the total training hours of those whose scores fall between the 25th and 75th percentile of all athletes in their respective sports?

If we create a composite ranking system where score accounts for 60% and inverse regional rank accounts for 40% (rank 1 = 15 points, rank 15 = 1 point), which sport has the highest average composite score among athletes who either train less than 35 hours OR are bonus eligible with scores above their sport's median?

title: Regional Sports Competition Results
questions: Among athletes from team sports (team size > 1) who are bonus eligible, what is the average score of those who either compete in the North region OR have a score above 90, but exclude any athlete whose sport starts with 'B' and whose score is below the overall average of all bonus-eligible team sport athletes?

For individual sports athletes (team size = 1) who are NOT bonus eligible, calculate the total number of athletes who satisfy this condition: they must be from either East or West regions AND have scores that rank in the top 3 within their specific sport category, but only count those whose regional average (for their region) exceeds 90 points?

What is the combined score total of athletes who meet ALL these criteria: they compete in sports where the regional representation (number of athletes from each region in that sport) is exactly 2, they are bonus eligible, their individual score exceeds the median score of all athletes in their region, and their sport has at least one non-bonus-eligible participant with a score above 90?

title: Multi-Sport Championship Results
questions: Among athletes who are bonus eligible and compete in individual sports (team size = 1), but excluding those ranked 1st in their region, what is the average score of those who scored above the median score of all bonus-eligible individual sport athletes?

For team sports where at least one athlete is not bonus eligible, calculate the weighted average score using regional rank as inverse weight (weight = 7 - rank), but only include athletes whose score exceeds the average score of bonus-eligible athletes in the same sport, then identify which sport has the highest weighted average?

Consider athletes in sports where the top regional performer (rank 1) is bonus eligible. Among these sports, find athletes who are either not bonus eligible OR have a regional rank worse than 3, then calculate how many of these athletes have scores that fall within one standard deviation of the mean score of all bonus-eligible athletes across all sports?

title: Soccer League Player Performance Statistics
questions: Among players who are bonus eligible and have played more than 2200 minutes, what is the average number of goals scored by those who either have more than 10 assists OR have zero red cards (but not both conditions), excluding any player whose team is either Eagles or Sharks?

For teams where at least 3 players are bonus eligible, calculate the total assists of players who have scored fewer than 15 goals AND have at most 1 red card, then determine which team has the highest such total, but only considering players who have played between 2000-2500 minutes?

What is the combined total of goals and assists for players who meet ALL of the following criteria: they are NOT bonus eligible, they have played more than the average minutes played across all players, their team has at least 2 players with 2+ red cards, and they personally have scored more goals than the median goals scored by bonus eligible players?

title: Soccer Player Performance Statistics
questions: Among players who are either forwards with more than 15 goals OR midfielders with more than 10 assists, but excluding those who played fewer than 2000 minutes, what is the average number of goals scored by bonus-eligible players in this filtered group?

For players who scored at least 10 goals AND have bonus eligibility, but are NOT goalkeepers, calculate the total assists of those whose minutes played exceed the median minutes played of all defenders in the dataset.

Among bonus-eligible players, identify those who either (scored more goals than the average goals of all forwards) OR (have more assists than the average assists of all midfielders), then exclude any player whose position is the same as the position with the lowest total minutes played across all positions. How many such players remain?

title: Soccer Player Performance Statistics
questions: Among forwards who are bonus eligible and have played more than 2000 minutes, what is the average number of total goal contributions (goals + assists) for those who have either scored more than 18 goals OR have more assists than goals, but exclude any player whose goal-to-assist ratio is exactly 3:1?

For midfielders who are not bonus eligible but have played at least 2000 minutes, compare their combined goals and assists total against bonus-eligible midfielders with fewer than 2500 minutes played. Which group has the higher average total contributions per player, and by how much?

If we create a composite performance score where goals are worth 3 points, assists worth 2 points, and there's a 20% bonus for players who are bonus eligible AND have played more than 2300 minutes, what is the total score difference between the top-scoring defender and the lowest-scoring forward who meets the bonus criteria?

title: Athlete Health and Fitness Assessment Data
questions: Among athletes who either have injury history AND compete in endurance sports (Running or Cycling) OR have no injury history AND compete in Swimming, what is the average VO2_Max of those whose Performance_Score exceeds the median Performance_Score of all athletes with Body_Fat_Percent below 8%, excluding any athlete whose VO2_Max is in the bottom 25% of their respective sport category?

For athletes competing in sports where the average Body_Fat_Percent of injury-free athletes is lower than 8%, identify those who have both above-median VO2_Max for their sport AND Performance_Score that ranks in the top 3 within their sport, then calculate how many of these athletes would maintain their top 3 ranking if all athletes with injury history in their sport had their Performance_Score increased by 5 points?

Consider athletes whose VO2_Max exceeds 70 OR whose Body_Fat_Percent is below 7%, but exclude those who have injury history AND Performance_Score below 90. Among the remaining athletes, group them by sport and calculate the weighted average Performance_Score (where VO2_Max serves as the weight), then determine which sport has the highest weighted average and by how much it exceeds the second-highest?

title: Elite Athlete Health and Fitness Assessment Data
questions: Among athletes who either have a VO2 Max above 70 OR have no injury history (but not both conditions simultaneously), and who also compete in sports other than Swimming, what is the average Performance Score of those whose Body Fat Percent is below the median Body Fat Percent of all athletes in their respective sport categories?

For athletes whose Performance Score exceeds the average Performance Score of athletes with injury history by at least 3 points, and who have either VO2 Max above 72 OR Body Fat Percent below 7% (but satisfy exactly one of these conditions), how many compete in Running compared to the total number of such qualified athletes?

If we create a composite fitness index by multiplying VO2 Max by Performance Score and dividing by Body Fat Percent, then filter for athletes who rank in the top 6 by this index AND have injury history, what is the difference between the highest and lowest VO2 Max values among athletes from the sport that appears most frequently in this filtered group?

title: Athlete Fitness Assessment Data
questions: Among athletes who either have no injury history OR have a VO2 max above 70 but not both conditions, and whose body fat percentage is below the average body fat of their respective sport, what is the average performance score of those who rank in the top 3 within their sport category?

For athletes with injury history who compete in sports where the median VO2 max exceeds 70, but excluding those whose performance score is within 2 points of their sport's average performance score, how many athletes would qualify if we additionally required their body fat percentage to be at least 1 standard deviation below their sport's mean body fat?

If we create composite fitness rankings by weighting VO2 max (40%), inverse body fat percentage (30%), and performance score (30%), then filter for athletes whose composite score exceeds the overall median composite score, and among these exclude athletes with injury history unless their performance score is above 90, what is the sport distribution of the remaining athletes?

title: Judge Scoring Records
questions: Among judges who scored either Figure Skating or Diving events, but not both, and who have a technical score above 8.0, what is the average artistic score for those who are bonus eligible and have senior experience level, excluding any judge whose combined technical and artistic scores exceed 18.0?

For judges scoring Gymnastics events with intermediate or senior experience levels, calculate the weighted composite score using the formula (Technical_Score × 0.6 + Artistic_Score × 0.4). Then, among those with composite scores above 8.0, what is the difference between the highest and lowest composite scores for bonus eligible judges versus non-bonus eligible judges?

Consider judges who meet all of the following criteria: (1) scored events other than Gymnastics, (2) have artistic scores greater than their technical scores, (3) are either senior level with bonus eligibility OR intermediate level without bonus eligibility, and (4) have a technical score between 7.5 and 9.0 inclusive. How many such judges have a combined score (technical + artistic) that ranks in the top 3 among all judges meeting these criteria?

title: Judge Scoring Records
questions: Among judges who scored either Figure Skating or Diving events (but not Gymnastics), and who are bonus eligible, what is the average Technical Score of those whose Artistic Score exceeds their Technical Score by at least 0.3 points, excluding any judge whose Final Rating is below the median Final Rating of all bonus-eligible judges across all events?

For judges who scored Gymnastics events with bonus eligibility, but whose Technical Score is higher than their Artistic Score, calculate the weighted average Final Rating where the weight is determined by the difference between Technical and Artistic scores, then compare this to the simple average Final Rating of non-bonus-eligible Figure Skating judges whose Artistic Score exceeds 8.5 - what is the absolute difference between these two values?

Identify judges who meet all of the following criteria: (1) scored events other than Diving, (2) have bonus eligibility, (3) their Final Rating is above the 75th percentile of all judges, and (4) the sum of their Technical and Artistic scores is greater than 17.0. Among these qualified judges, count how many have an Artistic Score that ranks in the top 3 when compared only against other judges from the same event type who also meet criteria 1-4.

title: Judge Scoring Records
questions: Among judges who scored either Figure Skating or Gymnastics events (but not Diving), and whose Technical Score is above 8.0, what is the average Final Rating for those who are bonus eligible, excluding any judge whose Artistic Score is below their Technical Score?

For judges who evaluated Gymnastics events with bonus eligibility, but whose Final Rating is either above 8.5 OR their Technical Score exceeds 9.0 (but not both conditions simultaneously), what is the total sum of their Technical Scores, excluding any judge whose Artistic Score is exactly equal to 8.0?

Among all judges whose Final Rating ranks in the top 50% within their respective event category, and who are either bonus eligible with Technical Score above 8.5 OR not bonus eligible with Artistic Score above 8.7, how many judges have a Technical Score that is lower than their Artistic Score?

title: Spring League Match Schedule
questions: Among teams that are playoff eligible with high league priority, considering only matches where they scored more than 25 points AND either had bonus points OR played in clear weather, what is the average attendance percentage (attendance/capacity) for teams that also had a referee rating above 8.0 but excluding any team that lost by more than 10 points?

For teams that played in non-clear weather conditions, if we only consider matches where the winning margin was less than 15 points AND the losing team had bonus points OR the stadium was more than 90% full, what is the total number of bonus points awarded to teams that also have medium or high league priority and referee ratings between 7.5 and 8.5 inclusive?

Among playoff eligible teams with high league priority, considering only home games (where Home_Score > Away_Score) that had either bonus points OR attendance above 50000, but excluding games with referee ratings below 8.0 OR where the winning margin exceeded 20 points, which team appears most frequently and how many times?

title: Team Match Schedules and Performance

What is the difference between the highest win rate among playoff eligible teams from North/South divisions with at least 8 home games, and the lowest win rate among non-playoff eligible teams from East/West divisions that have played more away games than home games and have a win rate above 0.45?

title: Team Match Schedule and Results
questions: Among playoff-eligible teams that scored more than 30 points in away games, what is the average point differential (points scored minus points allowed) for their home games only, excluding any games where they allowed more than 25 points at home?

For teams that are not playoff-eligible but won at least one away game (scored more than opponent), calculate the total points they scored in home games where they lost (allowed more points than scored), then subtract the number of such losing home games multiplied by 10?

Among all teams that played both home and away games, identify those where their best home performance (highest point differential) exceeds their worst away performance (lowest point differential) by more than 20 points, then count how many of these teams are playoff-eligible and had exactly 3 total games?

title: Professional Sports League Attendance Statistics
questions: Among teams with premium seats that have a win rate above 0.70, what is the average home attendance for those whose stadium capacity utilization (home attendance divided by stadium capacity) exceeds 0.85, but only if their away attendance is at least 90% of their home attendance?

What is the difference in average win rate between two groups: Group A consists of teams with premium seats whose home attendance exceeds away attendance by more than 4000, and Group B consists of teams without premium seats whose stadium capacity utilization is above 0.90?

title: Stadium Attendance and Pricing Data
questions: Among stadiums that have premium seating and charge more than $100 per ticket, what is the average attendance for those venues where the attendance rate (attendance/capacity) is either above 95% OR the venue hosts football games but not both conditions simultaneously?

For stadiums without premium seating that host either basketball or baseball games, calculate the total revenue potential (attendance × ticket price) only for venues where the ticket price is below the median ticket price of all stadiums in the dataset, then determine how many such venues have a capacity utilization rate above 90%?

Considering only football stadiums with premium seating where the ticket price exceeds $120, if we were to redistribute their total combined attendance equally among basketball venues that lack premium seating and have capacity below 20000, what would be the new average attendance per basketball venue, and how many football stadiums contributed to this calculation?

title: Stadium Spectator Attendance Statistics
questions: Among stadiums that either host football with premium seating OR host basketball as championship venues (but not both conditions), what is the total capacity of those venues where the average attendance exceeds 75% of their capacity, excluding any stadium with exactly 82500 capacity?

For venues that host championship events, calculate the average attendance rate (attendance/capacity) for each sport category, then identify which sport has the highest rate, but only considering stadiums where premium seating availability does NOT match whether their attendance exceeds the median attendance of all championship venues in the dataset?

If we create two groups - Group A: non-championship football stadiums with premium seating, and Group B: championship baseball stadiums without premium seating - what is the difference between the average capacity utilization rate of Group A versus Group B, considering only venues where the capacity is either above 60000 OR the attendance rate is below 80%?

title: Esports Tournament Player Performance Analysis

title: Esports Tournament Player Performance Analysis

title: Athletic Training Performance Log

For sites where heavy metals are detected AND the contamination status contradicts the heavy metal presence (i.e., status is 'Clean' despite heavy metals OR status is not 'Clean' despite no heavy metals), calculate the total nitrogen content, but exclude any site where the pH is either below 6.5 OR above 7.8, then determine how many such sites have phosphorus levels in the top 25% of the remaining filtered group.

Identify sites that meet ALL of the following compound criteria: (pH > 7.0 AND nitrogen < 50) OR (pH ≤ 7.0 AND phosphorus > 20), then among these, exclude sites with 'Severe' contamination status, group the remaining by heavy metal detection status, and report the difference between the maximum phosphorus level in the 'Yes' heavy metal group versus the 'No' heavy metal group.

title: Soil Contamination Assessment Data
questions: Among sites that either have pH below 6.0 OR heavy metal concentration above 80 ppm (but not both conditions simultaneously), and also have organic matter below 4%, what is the average heavy metal concentration for those that require remediation but are not classified as Critical contamination status?

For sites with moderate contamination status that don't require remediation, compare their average organic matter percentage to sites with high contamination status that do require remediation and have pH between 5.0-6.0. What is the difference in average organic matter percentage between these two groups?

If we implement a new policy where sites with pH above 7.0 AND organic matter above 5% would no longer require remediation regardless of current status, how many sites would change from requiring remediation to not requiring it, and what would be the total heavy metal concentration (sum) of all sites that would still require remediation after this policy change?
answers: 3 sites would change; total heavy metal concentration would be 722 ppm

title: Municipal Waste Disposal Facility Records
questions: Among facilities that handle either Plastic or Metal waste types, but exclude those using Landfill disposal method, calculate the average cost per ton for facilities that are Compliant AND have monthly volumes exceeding 200 tons, then identify how many facilities meet these criteria but have costs below this calculated average?

For facilities handling Organic waste that are either Non-Compliant OR use Composting method (but not both conditions simultaneously), determine the total monthly volume, then among all Hazardous waste facilities, count how many have individual monthly volumes that exceed 75% of this calculated Organic waste total?

Consider facilities where the cost per ton is above 100 AND the waste type is NOT Paper, then among these, identify facilities that are Compliant but have monthly volumes below the median volume of all Non-Compliant facilities in the dataset. What is the sum of monthly volumes for these qualifying facilities?

title: Waste Facility Disposal Records
questions: Among facilities that either handle more than 100 tons monthly OR have compliance scores above 90 (but not both conditions), and exclude those using landfill disposal, what is the total volume processed by permitted facilities that handle non-hazardous waste types?

For facilities with permits that handle recyclable materials (plastic, metal, glass, paper), but exclude those with compliance scores between 85-92 inclusive, what is the average monthly volume of facilities that use recycling as their primary disposal method and process more than 75 tons?

Among unpermitted facilities, identify those that either handle hazardous waste OR have compliance scores below 80, then exclude facilities using specialized disposal methods. What is the combined monthly volume of the remaining facilities that process more than 20 tons and have waste types that are not organic?

title: Municipal Waste Facility Processing Records
questions: Among facilities that handle either Hazardous or Medical waste types AND have emergency protocols in place, but NOT those using Recycling as disposal method, what is the average compliance score for facilities with monthly volumes exceeding the median volume of all Hazardous waste facilities?

For facilities processing Organic waste with compliance scores above 85, compare the total monthly volume of those using Composting versus Anaerobic Digestion methods, but exclude any facility that lacks emergency protocols AND has a volume below the average of all Electronic waste facilities. What is the difference in total volumes between these two disposal method groups?

If we rank all facilities by a composite score calculated as (Compliance_Score × 0.7 + Monthly_Volume_Tons × 0.3), then filter for facilities that either have emergency protocols OR handle Recyclable waste (but not both conditions simultaneously), and finally exclude those with disposal methods used by fewer than 3 facilities total, how many facilities remain in the top 50% of the composite score ranking?

title: Weather Station Monitoring Data
questions: Among stations with either high humidity (>70%) or high wind speed (>20 km/h) but not both conditions simultaneously, and excluding any station with critical alert status, what is the average temperature of those stations that also do not require maintenance?

For stations where the temperature exceeds 25°C and humidity is below 60%, calculate the total wind speed of stations that have either normal alert status with no maintenance required, or high alert status with maintenance required, but exclude any station where wind speed is exactly between 15-20 km/h inclusive?

Among stations that require maintenance, identify those with either temperature above 30°C or humidity above 80%, then from this subset, count only stations where the alert status is not normal, and the wind speed is either below 10 km/h or above 25 km/h, but exclude stations where both temperature exceeds 32°C and humidity is below 50%?

title: Regional Weather Station Monitoring Data
questions: Among stations with either high temperature (>30°C) or high humidity (>80%), but not both conditions simultaneously, calculate the average wind speed for those that also have precipitation below 2mm and are not in Critical alert status. What is this average rounded to one decimal place?

For stations that meet the criteria of having temperature between 15-25°C AND humidity above 70%, determine how many would change from Warning to Normal status if we applied a hypothetical rule where stations with wind speed above 20 km/h AND precipitation above 5mm remain Warning, while all others become Normal. What is the net change in Warning status count?

Create a composite risk score for each station using the formula: (Temperature deviation from 20°C × 0.3) + (Humidity × 0.2) + (Wind Speed × 0.1) + (Precipitation × 2). Among stations with Normal status, find those with risk scores in the top 25% of all Normal stations, then calculate what percentage of these high-risk Normal stations have wind speeds exceeding the median wind speed of all Critical status stations.

title: Weather Station Monitoring Data
questions: Among weather stations that either have Critical alert status OR require maintenance (but not both conditions simultaneously), and have wind speeds above the median wind speed of all stations, what is the average temperature of those stations that also have humidity levels below 60%?

For stations with Warning status that don't require maintenance, calculate the total wind speed. Then, among stations with Normal status that do require maintenance, find those with temperatures above 25°C. What is the ratio of the total wind speed of the Warning group to the count of qualifying Normal stations?

Consider stations where the temperature is above 25°C AND humidity is below 70%. From this group, exclude any station that has both Critical status AND requires maintenance. Among the remaining stations, rank them by a composite score (temperature × 0.4 + wind speed × 0.6). How many stations have a composite score above 20?

title: Industrial Facility Carbon Emission Records
questions: Among facilities that emit either CO2 or CH4 but not N2O, and have reduction targets above 20% or investments below 2 million USD (but not both conditions), what is the average monthly emissions of compliant facilities that also have emissions exceeding 1500 MT?

For facilities where the emission type is CO2 and compliance status is non-compliant, or where emission type is CH4 and reduction target exceeds 23%, calculate the total investment for those facilities that have monthly emissions between 1000-2500 MT and exclude any facility with the lowest investment amount in this filtered group?

Consider facilities that are either (compliant with reduction targets ≥18% and emissions >1200 MT) or (non-compliant with investments ≥3 million USD). Among these, rank by emission intensity (emissions per investment dollar) and identify how many facilities fall into the top 40% of this ranking while also having CH4 or CO2 emission types?

title: Corporate Carbon Emission and Investment Records 2023
questions: Among companies that either have renewable energy percentage above 50% OR carbon offset investment above 3 million USD (but not both conditions simultaneously), and are in Manufacturing or Energy industries, what is the average CO2 emissions of those that are compliant but exclude any company whose carbon offset investment per ton of CO2 emissions exceeds 70 USD per ton?

For non-compliant companies in Transportation industry, if we hypothetically required them to increase their carbon offset investment to match the average investment-to-emissions ratio of compliant Energy companies (USD per MT CO2), what would be the total additional investment needed, but only considering companies whose current renewable energy percentage is below the median renewable energy percentage of all Transportation companies?

Among compliant companies, create two groups: Group A contains companies with above-median CO2 emissions AND below-median renewable energy percentage, Group B contains companies with below-median CO2 emissions AND above-median renewable energy percentage. Which group has a higher average carbon offset investment per company, and what is the difference in USD?

title: Corporate Carbon Emission Records 2023
questions: Among companies that either have renewable energy percentage above 50% OR participate in carbon offset programs (but not both conditions simultaneously), and are currently non-compliant, what is the total CO2 emissions of those in the Energy sector excluding any company with emissions below 40000 tons?

For compliant companies in Manufacturing and Transportation sectors combined, if we exclude those with both renewable energy below 30% AND no carbon offset program, then rank the remaining companies by a composite environmental score (calculated as: renewable energy percentage minus emissions per 1000 tons), what is the Company_ID of the second-ranked company?

Consider companies that meet exactly two of these three criteria: (1) emissions above 15000 tons, (2) renewable energy percentage above 40%, (3) participation in carbon offset programs. Among these filtered companies, if we group them by compliance status and calculate the average emissions per group, what is the difference in average emissions between compliant and non-compliant groups?

title: Environmental Complaint Resolution Log
questions: Among complaints with severity scores above 6.0 that either involve Air or Water pollution (but not both types simultaneously per complaint), what is the average resolution time for those that have High community impact and are resolved, excluding any cases where the resolution time exceeds the median resolution time of all High impact resolved complaints?

For pollution types where at least 2 complaints exist with Medium community impact, calculate the ratio of average severity scores between resolved complaints with resolution times under 30 days versus those with resolution times of 30 days or more, but only include pollution types where this ratio is greater than 1.0. What is the sum of these ratios?

Consider complaints that are either (High severity score above 7.0 AND High community impact) OR (Medium community impact AND resolution time below 25 days). Among these, exclude any Air pollution complaints where the severity score is the highest within Air pollution complaints. For the remaining complaints, group by resolution status and calculate the difference between the maximum and minimum days to resolution within each group. What is the larger of these two differences?

title: Environmental Complaint Resolution Log
questions: Among complaints with severity scores above 8.0 that either required follow-up OR took more than 50 days to resolve (but not both conditions), what is the average compensation awarded to those involving Air Pollution or Water Contamination issues, excluding any cases where the days to resolution exactly match the severity score multiplied by 10?

For complaint types that have at least 3 cases in the dataset, calculate the weighted average compensation where the weight is the severity score, but only include cases that meet this compound criteria: (severity > 7.5 AND follow-up required) OR (severity ≤ 7.5 AND days to resolution < 30 AND compensation > 1000). What is the highest weighted average among these complaint types?

Consider complaints that fall into exactly one of these categories: (1) high severity with follow-up (severity ≥ 8.5 AND follow-up required), (2) medium severity with quick resolution (6.0 ≤ severity < 8.5 AND days ≤ 30), or (3) low compensation with long resolution (compensation ≤ 1000 AND days > 40). Among these filtered complaints, rank the issue types by their total compensation and return the count of complaints for the issue type with the second-highest total compensation.

title: Environmental Complaint Resolution Log
questions: Among complaints with severity scores above 7.5 that are either Air pollution from repeat offenders OR Water pollution cases that took more than 15 days to resolve, what is the average fine amount for those where the fine exceeds the median fine of all qualifying cases?

For pollution types where at least 2 repeat offenders exist with severity scores above 6.0, calculate the total fine amount for non-repeat offenders in those same pollution types, but only include cases where days to resolution is below the average resolution time of repeat offenders in that pollution type category.

What is the difference between the highest fine amount among cases that meet ALL of these criteria: (severity score > 8.0 AND repeat offender = Yes) OR (pollution type = Soil AND days to resolution > 20), versus the lowest fine amount among cases that are either high-severity Air pollution (score > 8.0) with resolution time under 15 days, or Water pollution repeat offenders with fines above 15000?

title: Monthly Energy Consumption and Efficiency Report
questions: Among facilities using renewable energy sources (Solar, Wind, Hydroelectric) with efficiency ratings above 8.5 OR those using non-renewable sources with carbon offset programs, calculate the average monthly consumption for facilities that have peak hours usage below 50% AND exclude any facility whose consumption exceeds the median consumption of all qualifying facilities by more than 100 MWh?

For facilities that either have efficiency ratings in the top 25% of all facilities OR participate in carbon offset programs but NOT both conditions simultaneously, determine how many of these facilities would need to reduce their peak hours usage to below 40% to achieve a group average peak hours usage of exactly 35%, assuming facilities with the highest current peak hours usage are prioritized for reduction?

If we create two groups - Group A: renewable energy facilities with efficiency ratings below 9.0 that don't participate in carbon offset programs, and Group B: non-renewable facilities with efficiency ratings above 6.0 that do participate in carbon offset programs - what is the difference in total monthly consumption between the group with higher average efficiency rating and the group with lower average efficiency rating?

title: Building Energy Consumption Log
questions: Among buildings with efficiency ratings of A or better that use either Solar or Hybrid energy, but excluding those with peak hour usage above 25%, what is the total monthly cost for buildings where the monthly consumption exceeds the average consumption of all Solar buildings in the dataset?

For buildings using Grid energy with efficiency ratings worse than B, calculate the weighted average cost per building (consumption × cost per kWh), then identify how many Hybrid buildings have both lower individual costs than this weighted average AND peak hour usage between 25-35% inclusive?

If we group buildings by energy type and consider only those with peak hour usage below 30%, then within each group select buildings with above-median consumption for that group, what is the difference between the highest and lowest total monthly costs among these selected buildings?

title: Building Energy Consumption Log
questions: Among buildings that use renewable energy sources (Solar or Wind) and have either efficiency rating A with peak usage below 10 hours OR efficiency rating B with consumption above 2500 kWh, what is the total monthly cost for buildings whose cost per kWh is exactly 0.12 and peak usage is not equal to 8 hours?

For buildings with Grid energy type that have efficiency rating B or C, calculate the average consumption of those buildings whose peak usage hours exceed the median peak usage hours of all Wind energy buildings, but exclude any building whose consumption multiplied by cost per kWh results in a monthly cost above 700.

Among buildings where the energy type is Solar and efficiency rating is A, or energy type is Wind with peak usage between 7-11 hours inclusive, identify buildings whose consumption is above the average consumption of all Grid buildings with efficiency rating C, then determine how many of these identified buildings have a cost per kWh that is lower than the maximum cost per kWh of all Wind buildings?

title: Environmental Risk Assessment Data
questions: Among sites with contamination levels above 50 AND population density greater than 1500, but excluding those with pending monitoring status, what is the average risk score for sites that require remediation but have risk scores below 8.5?

For sites where either the contamination level exceeds 60 OR the population density is above 2500 (but not both conditions simultaneously), and the monitoring status is active, how many sites require remediation AND have risk scores that fall within the range of the median risk score ± 1.0 of all qualifying sites?

If we group sites by whether they require remediation, then within each group exclude sites with inactive monitoring status, what is the difference between the highest contamination level in the 'Yes' remediation group versus the lowest contamination level in the 'No' remediation group, considering only sites where population density multiplied by risk score exceeds 5000?

title: Environmental Risk Assessment Data
questions: What is the average remediation cost for sites that are either in Critical risk category with population density above 2000 OR in High risk category with pollution levels between 70-80, but excluding any sites that are compliant and have remediation costs below 200000?

Among non-compliant sites with pollution levels above 60, calculate the total population exposure (sum of population densities) for sites where the remediation cost per person (cost divided by population density) is greater than the overall average remediation cost per person across all medium and high risk sites, but only if the site's pollution level exceeds the median pollution level of critical sites?

For sites that meet the criteria of being either (High risk AND non-compliant AND population density > 1200) OR (Critical risk AND remediation cost > 400000), determine how many of these sites would change their priority ranking if we applied a composite risk score calculated as (Pollution_Level × 0.4 + Population_Density/10 × 0.6), then ranked them, and compared against their current risk category hierarchy (Critical > High > Medium > Low)?

title: Environmental Risk Assessment Sites
questions: Among sites with contamination levels above 7.0 that have either high ecological sensitivity OR population density exceeding 3000, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, what is the average remediation cost for those classified as critical regulatory priority, excluding any site where the cost per contamination unit exceeds 65000?

For sites with medium ecological sensitivity and high regulatory priority, calculate the total population exposure risk (contamination level × population density) for those sites where the remediation cost is below the median cost of all medium sensitivity sites, then determine how many sites contribute more than 15000 to this total risk score?

Among critical priority sites with contamination levels between 7.5 and 9.0, identify those where the cost-effectiveness ratio (remediation cost divided by contamination level) ranks in the bottom 40% of all critical sites, then calculate what percentage of the total population density these sites represent relative to all sites with population density above 2000?

title: Air Quality Monitoring Stations Data
questions: Among stations in industrial zones with Red or Orange alert status, what is the average PM2.5 level for those stations that also have population density above 2500 and ozone levels exceeding 100, but excluding any station where the PM2.5 level is below 60?

How many stations have either (Yellow alert status with population density below 2000 and are not in industrial zones) OR (Green alert status with PM2.5 levels above 30 and ozone levels below 50), but specifically excluding any station that has both PM2.5 above 40 AND is in an industrial zone?

What is the total population density across all stations that meet the following compound criteria: they must have Orange alert status AND be in industrial zones AND have ozone levels between 90-110, BUT only if their PM2.5 level exceeds the average PM2.5 of all Green status stations by at least 20 points?

title: Bank Transaction Statement with Customer Tiers
questions: Among customers with Gold or Platinum tier status who have either Checking accounts with amounts over $2000 OR Business accounts with fee waivers, but excluding those with monthly balances below $20000, what is the average transaction amount for the subset that has both fee waivers AND monthly balances exceeding the median balance of all qualifying transactions?

For transactions where the account type is NOT Savings, and the customer tier is either Silver with fee waived OR Bronze with amounts above $300, calculate the total transaction value, then determine how many of these transactions would still qualify if we hypothetically changed the fee waiver status of all Bronze customers to 'Yes' and required monthly balances to exceed $10000?

Consider Business account holders with Platinum tier who have fee waivers, and Checking account holders with Gold tier whose amounts exceed $1500. Between these two groups, which group has a higher ratio of average transaction amount to average monthly balance, and what is the difference in this ratio expressed as a percentage?

title: Bank Transaction Statement with Customer Tiers
questions: Among customers with either Gold or Platinum tier status, but excluding those with Business accounts that have monthly balances exceeding 50000, what is the average transaction amount for transactions where fees were waived and the transaction amount is greater than the median transaction amount of all Silver tier customers?

For accounts where the customer tier is not Bronze and the account type is either Checking or Savings, but only if the monthly balance is at least 3 times the transaction amount, calculate the total transaction amount for cases where fees were not waived, then determine how many such transactions exceed 80% of this total divided by the number of qualifying transactions?

Consider only transactions from customers whose tier matches their account performance (Gold/Platinum tiers with monthly balance > 20000, or Silver/Bronze with balance ≤ 20000), then among those with fee waiver status opposite to the majority fee waiver pattern in their tier group, what is the sum of transaction amounts for Business accounts minus the sum for non-Business accounts?

title: Bank Transaction Statement with Account Details
questions: Among transactions where fees were applied, what is the average transaction amount for accounts that have either Gold or Platinum status, but only if their monthly volume exceeds 20000 and the account type is not Savings, excluding any Business accounts with amounts below 4000?

For non-Investment accounts with Bronze or Silver status, calculate the total monthly volume of transactions that either have no fees applied OR have amounts greater than 1500, then subtract the count of Checking accounts in this subset that have fees applied and amounts below 2000?

What is the difference between the highest transaction amount among Platinum status accounts with fees applied and monthly volumes above 50000, versus the average amount of Gold status transactions that have no fees but monthly volumes between 15000 and 40000, excluding any account types that appear less than 2 times in the filtered Gold subset?

title: Credit Card Billing Details
questions: Among customers who either have Premium cards with no late payments OR Gold cards with late payments, but excluding those whose monthly spend exceeds 80% of their credit limit, what is the average reward points for customers whose monthly spend is above the median spend of their respective customer type group?

For customers whose reward points per dollar spent is above 1.5 AND who belong to customer types where at least 40% of members have late payments, calculate the total credit limit of those customers whose monthly spend ranks in the top 3 within their customer type, but only if their credit utilization is below 25%.

Among Premium customers without late payments whose credit utilization is below 30%, and Gold customers with late payments whose monthly spend exceeds $2000, determine how many customers would qualify for a bonus program that requires either being in the top 2 spenders of their type OR having reward points that exceed 150% of their customer type's average, but not both conditions simultaneously.

title: Credit Card Customer Portfolio
questions: Among customers with either Gold or Platinum tier cards who have monthly spending above $3000, but excluding those with more than 1 late payment, what is the average credit utilization ratio (monthly spend divided by credit limit) for cards that have annual fees greater than $50?

For customers whose credit utilization is below 40% AND who either have zero late payments OR belong to Platinum tier (but not both conditions simultaneously), calculate the total monthly spending of those whose annual fee is exactly divisible by their late payment count plus one, excluding Bronze tier customers?

Among all customers who have monthly spending that exceeds 25% of their credit limit, identify those who either pay annual fees OR have made late payments, then from this group, exclude customers whose rewards tier alphabetically comes before 'Silver', and finally calculate how many such customers have credit limits that are multiples of 1000?

title: Credit Card Customer Billing Analysis
questions: Among customers who have either Premium cards with monthly spending above $4000 OR Gold cards with credit limits above $12000, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, what is the average reward points for those who also maintain on-time payment status and have reward points that exceed twice their monthly spending divided by 1000?

For customers whose card type is not Standard, calculate the total monthly spending of those who meet ALL of the following criteria: their credit utilization ratio (monthly spend / credit limit) is below 0.25, they have on-time payments, their reward points are at least 1.5 times their monthly spending, and they belong to the card type that has the highest average credit limit among non-Standard cards?

What is the difference in total reward points between two groups: Group A consists of customers with late payments who have Premium or Gold cards and monthly spending above the median spending of all on-time Premium customers, versus Group B which includes Standard card holders with on-time payments whose reward points exceed the average reward points of all late-paying customers by at least 500 points?

title: Loan Approval Applications
questions: Among applicants who either have collateral OR earn above $80,000 annually (but not both conditions), and whose credit score exceeds 700, what is the average loan amount for those whose employment status is NOT contract work?

For applicants with credit scores between 650-750 who have collateral, compare the total loan amounts between full-time employees versus non-full-time employees, then determine how much higher the larger group's total is than the smaller group's total?

If we rank applicants by their debt-to-income ratio (loan amount divided by annual income), but only consider those who either lack collateral AND work part-time, OR have collateral AND work full-time, what is the applicant ID of the person ranked 3rd highest in this filtered and ranked list?

title: Loan Application Assessment Data
questions: Among applicants who either have collateral OR earn above 80000 annually (but not both conditions), and whose credit score exceeds 650, what is the average loan amount for those in full-time employment, excluding any applicant whose loan-to-income ratio exceeds 3.0?

For applicants with credit scores between 600-750 who are NOT in full-time employment, calculate the total loan amount for those who satisfy exactly one of these conditions: (1) have collateral, (2) earn more than 50000 annually, (3) request loans above 150000, then determine how many such applicants have loan-to-income ratios below 2.5?

If we modify the approval criteria such that part-time workers need collateral AND credit scores above 700 to qualify, while contract workers need either high income (>70000) OR collateral (but not both), how many currently qualifying full-time applicants would still maintain the lowest risk profile (top 25% by credit score AND loan-to-income ratio below 2.8)?

title: Loan Application Assessment Database
questions: Among applicants with credit scores above 700 who either have collateral OR work full-time (but not both), and whose debt-to-income ratio is below 0.40, what is the average loan amount for those who were approved, excluding any applicants with previous defaults?

For contract workers with credit scores between 650-720 who have collateral, compare the total loan amount requested by those with zero previous defaults versus those with exactly one previous default, but only consider applications that are either approved or pending, and exclude any applicant whose debt-to-income ratio exceeds 0.45.

What is the difference in average annual income between two groups: (Group A) full-time employees with credit scores above 700, no previous defaults, and approved status; versus (Group B) all other applicants who have collateral, credit scores above 680, and were either approved or have pending status, excluding anyone with more than one previous default?

title: Corporate Financial Performance Analysis
questions: Among companies with revenue above 2000 million that either have dividends OR credit rating of AA (but not both conditions), and excluding those with debt ratio above 0.4, what is the average profit margin of the remaining companies after removing the company with the highest debt ratio from this filtered group?

For companies that have no dividends AND profit margin above 15%, calculate the total revenue of those with credit rating A or better, then subtract the revenue of companies in this same filtered group that have debt ratio above 0.3. What is the final amount?

Identify companies with debt ratio below 0.5 that have either (dividends AND credit rating BBB or better) OR (no dividends AND profit margin above 20%). From this group, exclude any company whose revenue is in the bottom 25% of all companies in the table. How many companies remain after applying all these filters?

title: Corporate Financial Performance Analysis
questions: Among companies with credit ratings of A or higher that pay dividends, what is the average profit margin of those companies whose debt ratio is below the median debt ratio of all dividend-paying companies with investment-grade ratings (BBB or better), excluding any company whose revenue exceeds the 75th percentile of all companies in the dataset?

For companies that either have a profit margin above 10% OR pay dividends (but not both conditions simultaneously), calculate the total revenue of those companies whose debt ratio is lower than the average debt ratio of non-dividend-paying companies, but only include companies whose credit rating is better than the worst rating among companies with revenue above 1500 million?

What is the weighted average debt ratio of companies that satisfy all of the following: have investment-grade credit ratings, generate revenue between the 25th and 75th percentiles of all companies, and either pay dividends with profit margins below 12% OR don't pay dividends with profit margins above 8%, where the weights are determined by each company's revenue as a proportion of the total revenue of this filtered group?

title: Corporate Financial Performance Analysis
questions: Among companies that either pay dividends OR have operating margins above 20% (but not both conditions), and excluding those in Banking or Energy sectors, what is the total revenue of companies with debt ratios below 0.4?

For companies in Technology and Healthcare sectors combined, if we rank them by a composite score calculated as (Operating_Margin_Pct × 2 + (1-Debt_Ratio) × 100), what is the revenue difference between the highest and lowest scoring dividend-paying companies?

Considering only companies with revenues above $1000M that don't pay dividends, and comparing the average operating margin of those in high-debt industries (where average sector debt ratio ≥ 0.5) versus low-debt industries, what is the absolute difference in average operating margins between these two groups?

title: Stock Trading Performance Records
questions: Among traders who are bonus eligible and have a risk rating of 5 or lower, but excluding those with negative profit/loss, what is the average trade volume for traders whose profit exceeds 8000 OR whose risk rating is exactly 3, but not both conditions simultaneously?

For traders with trade volumes above 10000 who are either not bonus eligible OR have risk ratings above 6, calculate the total profit/loss, then subtract the sum of trade volumes for profitable traders (profit > 0) within this group who have risk ratings of exactly 7 or 8.

Identify traders who meet ALL of the following: bonus eligible, risk rating between 3-5 inclusive, and trade volume above the median volume of all profitable traders. Among these qualified traders, what is the difference between the highest and lowest profit/loss values?

title: Stock Trading Records
questions: Among traders who made both buy and sell transactions for the same stock symbol, what is the total trade volume for buy transactions of stocks where the average commission rate across all transactions (both buy and sell) for that stock is greater than 0.27%, but only considering traders whose total transaction value (volume × price) across all their trades exceeds $500,000?

For stock symbols that have been traded by at least 3 different traders, calculate the weighted average price per share (weighted by trade volume) for sell transactions only, then identify which stock has the highest ratio of this weighted average sell price to the simple average buy price, but exclude any stock where the total sell volume exceeds the total buy volume by more than 500 shares?

What is the combined commission fee earned from traders who have executed trades in exactly 2 different stock symbols, where at least one of those symbols has a commission rate difference of more than 0.05% between its highest and lowest commission rates across all traders, and the trader's total buy volume is greater than their total sell volume, but only counting trades where the price per share is within the middle 50% range of all prices for that specific stock symbol?

title: Stock Trading Records Q4 2023
questions: Among traders who are bonus eligible and made profitable trades, what is the average trade volume for those who either bought stocks with profit exceeding $10,000 OR sold stocks with volumes above 1,500 shares, but excluding any trader whose profit-to-volume ratio is below 8?

For traders who are NOT bonus eligible, how many of them have losses that exceed the average loss of all bonus-eligible traders who made losing trades, while also having trade volumes that fall within the middle 50% range of all buy transactions?

What is the total profit of traders who satisfy ALL of the following: are bonus eligible, have trade volumes exceeding the median volume of sell transactions, made profitable trades, and whose profit per share is greater than the average profit per share of all losing buy transactions (treating losses as negative profit per share)?

title: Insurance Claim Processing Records
questions: Among claims that are either from Premium customers with processing times under 20 days OR from Gold customers with claim amounts above 10000, but excluding any Life insurance claims that took more than 40 days to process, what is the average claim amount for the remaining settled claims?

For customers who have either Auto claims above 15000 OR Health claims below 4000, but not both types simultaneously, and whose claims were processed in under 25 days, how many of these customers had their claims settled versus denied, considering only Standard and Gold tier customers?

What is the total claim amount for policies where the customer tier is Premium AND the claim is settled, OR the customer tier is Gold AND the processing days exceed 25, but excluding any Home insurance claims that were denied and any Auto claims from Standard customers that took more than 15 days to process?

title: Insurance Claim Processing Records
questions: Among claims that are either settled Auto claims with processing time under 50 days OR pending Home claims with amounts above 15000, but NOT claims from Bronze tier policies, what is the average claim amount for those that also have processing times that exceed the median processing time of all Gold tier settled claims?

For policy types where the total settled claim amount exceeds 60000 AND the average processing time for denied claims in that type is greater than 70 days, what is the difference between the highest and lowest claim amounts among pending claims in those policy types, excluding any claims from Silver tier policies?

Consider claims that meet ALL of the following: (1) either Gold or Platinum tier, (2) processing time between 20-80 days, (3) NOT denied status, and (4) from policy types where at least 2 claims exist in the dataset. Among these filtered claims, if we rank policy types by their average claim amount in descending order, what is the claim amount of the second-highest individual claim from the policy type that ranks third?

title: Insurance Claim Processing Records
questions: Among claims that were either approved with a risk score below 4.0 OR denied with processing time exceeding 20 days, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, what is the average claim amount for Auto and Health policies combined, excluding any Life policy claims?

For policy types where the total approved claim amount exceeds $50,000, calculate the weighted average processing days using claim amounts as weights, but only include claims with risk scores between 2.0 and 5.0 that were processed in under 30 days, then subtract the count of denied claims in those same policy types.

If we group claims by policy type and consider only those types where at least 2 claims were approved AND the maximum risk score among approved claims is less than 6.0, what is the ratio of the highest total claim amount to the lowest total claim amount among these qualifying policy types?

title: Invoice Payment Records
questions: Among invoices that are either overdue with more than 30 days OR pending with discount eligibility, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, what is the total amount for Premium clients only, excluding any Basic client invoices that have amounts below the average amount of all Standard client invoices?

For clients who have both paid invoices and either overdue or pending invoices, calculate the weighted average amount where paid invoices get 70% weight and non-paid invoices get 30% weight, then identify which client type has the highest such weighted average, but only consider client types that have at least 2 invoices in each payment status category?

If we implement a new policy where discount eligibility is revoked for any invoice that is overdue by more than 35 days, and then calculate a risk score as (Amount × Days_Overdue ÷ 1000) for remaining discount-eligible invoices, what would be the total risk score for the top 3 highest-amount invoices that maintain discount eligibility under this new policy?

title: Invoice Payment Records
questions: Among invoices where either the client is Premium with discount applied OR the client is Standard without discount but amount exceeds 10000, and excluding any invoices that are both overdue by more than 25 days AND have amounts below 15000, what is the average amount of the remaining invoices that are either Paid or have days overdue less than 20?

For invoices that satisfy the condition of being either (Premium clients with amounts above 18000) or (non-Premium clients with discount applied and pending status), but excluding those that are simultaneously overdue by more than 50 days and have Basic client type, calculate the total amount difference between invoices with discount applied versus those without discount applied within this filtered set?

Consider invoices that meet the criteria of either having (Standard client type with overdue status and amount between 7000-12000) or (Premium client type with paid status and no discount), then exclude any that have days overdue exactly 0 AND amount below 16000, and finally count how many of the remaining invoices have either pending status OR days overdue greater than 30?

title: Invoice Payment Records
questions: Among clients who either have Premium status with discounts applied OR Standard status with amounts exceeding 10000, but excluding those with overdue payments beyond 25 days, what is the total amount of invoices that are either Paid or have been pending for less than 12 days?

For invoices where the client type is not Basic, calculate the average amount of invoices that satisfy the following compound condition: (Payment status is Overdue AND days overdue is between 20-50) OR (Payment status is Pending AND discount was applied AND amount is above 15000). How many invoices meet this criteria?
