Among all invoices with discounts applied, identify those belonging to clients who are either Premium with amounts above 20000 OR Standard with overdue payments less than 40 days, then exclude any that are currently Paid, and finally determine what percentage of the remaining invoices have amounts that exceed the average amount of all Basic client invoices?

title: Tax Filing Analysis Dataset
questions: Among taxpayers with filing status of either Single or Head of Household, who have gross income above $60,000 but below $100,000, and whose deductions claimed represent more than 18% of their gross income, what is the average audit risk score for those whose tax owed is less than the median tax owed of all taxpayers in this filtered group?

For married taxpayers (both Joint and Separate filers) whose audit risk score exceeds 3.0, calculate the total tax owed by those whose deduction-to-income ratio is either in the top 25% or bottom 25% among all married filers, but exclude any taxpayer whose gross income is within 10% of the overall average gross income of married filers with audit risk above 3.0.

Identify taxpayers whose tax owed per $1000 of gross income is above the 75th percentile among their respective filing status group, then among these high-burden taxpayers, find those whose audit risk score is below the average audit risk of taxpayers in the same filing status with deductions exceeding $15,000, and calculate the sum of their gross incomes minus their total deductions claimed.

title: Tax Filing Analysis Dataset
questions: Among taxpayers with either Single or Head_of_Household filing status, who have AGI between 50000 and 100000, and whose tax credits exceed 2000 but deductions are less than 15000, what is the average AGI of those classified as Medium or High audit risk, excluding any taxpayer whose credits-to-deductions ratio is greater than 0.25?

For married taxpayers (either Joint or Separate filing), calculate the total tax credits of those whose AGI is above the median AGI of all Single filers, but only include taxpayers whose deductions are at least 1.5 times their credits, and whose audit risk is not Low, then subtract the count of such taxpayers multiplied by 1000?

Identify taxpayers whose AGI falls in the top 30% of their respective filing status group, have audit risk of Medium or High, and whose combined credits plus deductions exceed 20000. Among these, find those whose credits represent more than 15% of their deductions, then calculate the difference between the highest and lowest AGI in this final subset?

title: Tax Filing Risk Assessment Database
questions: Among taxpayers who are either single with gross income above $50,000 OR married filing separately with deductions exceeding $10,000, but NOT those with audit risk scores in the top 25% of all taxpayers, what is the average tax credit amount for those whose effective deduction rate (deductions/gross income) is below the median effective deduction rate of the entire dataset?

For taxpayers whose filing status is not 'Single' and who have audit risk scores below the 75th percentile, calculate the total gross income of those whose tax credits are above the average tax credits of married filing jointly taxpayers, but exclude any taxpayer whose deduction amount ranks in the bottom 30% among all non-single filers.

What is the count of taxpayers who satisfy ALL of the following compound conditions: (1) their gross income is above the median gross income of their filing status group, (2) their audit risk score is either below 20 OR above 25 but not between 20-25 inclusive, (3) their tax credits exceed 150% of the average tax credits for their income bracket (defined as: low <$50k, medium $50k-$80k, high >$80k), and (4) their deduction-to-income ratio is within one standard deviation of the mean ratio for all taxpayers?

title: Annual Department Budget Performance Analysis
questions: Among departments with High priority that are bonus eligible and have performance scores above 85, what is the total budget variance (allocated minus spent) for those departments that spent less than 97% of their allocated budget?

For departments that are either bonus eligible with Medium priority OR have performance scores above 90 but NOT both conditions simultaneously, calculate the average performance score of those departments whose actual spending exceeds 95% of their allocated budget.

What is the weighted performance score for High priority departments, where the weight is determined by budget utilization rate (actual spent / allocated), but only including departments that are bonus eligible and excluding any department whose performance score is exactly the median performance score of all bonus eligible departments?

title: Corporate Department Budget Performance Analysis
questions: What is the total budget variance (allocated minus actual spend) for departments that either have a bonus pool and performance score above 8.0, OR are classified as Critical priority but do NOT have a bonus pool, excluding any department where the actual spend exceeds the allocated budget by more than 5%?

Among departments with High or Critical priority levels, what is the average performance score of those that have a bonus pool and stayed within 95% of their allocated budget, compared to those that either lack a bonus pool OR exceeded 97% of their allocated budget?

If we were to redistribute 10% of the total budget variance (where actual spend was less than allocated) from Low priority departments to Critical priority departments that have both a bonus pool and performance score below 8.5, how much additional funding would each qualifying Critical department receive on average?

title: Annual Department Budget Performance Analysis
questions: Among departments with Critical or High priority that are bonus eligible and have performance scores above 85, what is the total budget variance (difference between allocated and spent) for those that either overspent by more than 5% OR underspent by more than 10%, excluding any department where the actual spending falls between 90% and 105% of allocated budget?

For departments that are NOT bonus eligible but have performance scores above the median score of all bonus-eligible departments, calculate the average budget utilization rate (actual spent / budget allocated), but only include departments where the priority level is either Medium or High AND the absolute budget variance exceeds $5000?

What is the weighted performance score for Critical priority departments that are bonus eligible, where the weight is determined by their budget allocation relative to the total budget of all Critical priority departments, but exclude any department that both overspent their budget AND has a performance score below 90?

title: Personal Asset Registration Portfolio
questions: Among clients who are either premium members with risk scores above 7.0 OR non-premium members with asset values exceeding $150,000, but excluding those with suspended status, what is the average asset value of clients who have been active for more than 2 years and have active registration status?

For clients with active registration status, calculate the total asset value of premium members whose risk score is between 6.0 and 8.5 (inclusive), then subtract the total asset value of non-premium members in the same risk score range who have been active for less than 3 years. What is the resulting difference?

Among all clients who satisfy the condition of having either (premium membership AND risk score > 8.0) OR (asset value > $200,000 AND years active ≥ 5), but excluding any client with pending status, how many clients have risk scores that fall within one standard deviation of the group's mean risk score?

title: Personal Asset Registration Portfolio
questions: Among clients with Active registration status who are bonus eligible, what is the total asset value of those holding either Real Estate OR Cryptocurrency assets, but excluding any client whose risk score falls between 7.0 and 8.0 (inclusive), and then calculate the average asset value within this filtered group?

For clients holding Stocks or Bonds with asset values exceeding $150,000, identify those who are either (bonus eligible AND have Active status) OR (not bonus eligible BUT have Pending status), exclude any with risk scores below 5.0, then determine how many such clients have risk scores in the top 50% of this filtered subset?

Consider only clients with Suspended status OR those with Active status who hold Cryptocurrency. Among these, identify clients who are bonus eligible AND have asset values above $200,000, then exclude those with risk scores above 8.5. What is the difference between the highest and lowest asset values in this final filtered group?

title: Personal Asset Registration Portfolio
questions: Among clients with Active registration status who are bonus eligible, what is the total asset value of those holding either Real Estate OR Stocks (but not both asset types if they appear multiple times), excluding any client whose risk score is above 7.5 OR whose asset value is below 100000?

For clients whose registration status is NOT Suspended AND who have risk scores between 6.0 and 8.0 (inclusive), calculate the average asset value separately for bonus eligible and non-bonus eligible groups, then determine how many clients fall into the group with the higher average?

Consider only Active clients with Bonds OR Cryptocurrency assets whose risk scores are either below 5.0 OR above 8.5, but exclude any client who is bonus eligible AND has an asset value exceeding 150000. What is the combined asset value of the remaining clients after applying a hypothetical 15% portfolio adjustment factor?

title: Citizen ID Registration Records
questions: Among citizens who registered in even-numbered years (2018, 2020) and either live in Downtown with income above 50000 OR live in Industrial districts with dependents, what is the average age at registration for those whose income is below the median income of all citizens in their respective districts?

For citizens who registered after 2018 and are either (under 30 years old with dependents) OR (over 35 years old without dependents), calculate the total income of those living in districts where the average income of citizens with dependents exceeds 45000, but exclude any citizen whose age at registration is exactly the mode age across all Rural district registrations.

Consider citizens who registered in 2019 or 2021 and live in non-Downtown districts. Among those whose income rank within their district is in the top 50% AND who either have dependents or are aged between 25-35, what is the income difference between the highest and lowest earners, excluding anyone whose registration year matches the year when the maximum number of Rural citizens registered?

title: Citizen ID Registration Records
questions: Among citizens registered in 2018 or 2020 who are either from Downtown with income above 80000 or from Rural areas with dependents, but excluding those who are both over 40 years old AND have income below 50000, what is the average income of the remaining eligible citizens?

For citizens registered in odd-numbered years (2019, 2021) who are either under 35 with no dependents OR over 40 with dependents, calculate the total count after excluding Downtown residents with income above 90000, then determine how many of these remaining citizens are from Suburb districts?

Consider citizens who meet exactly one of these criteria: (registered in 2018-2019 AND age 30-40) OR (from Rural/Suburb AND has dependents). Among this group, exclude those with income between 40000-60000, then rank the remaining citizens by income and identify the citizen ID of the person with the 3rd highest income.

title: Citizen ID Registration Records
questions: Among citizens who registered in February 2023 and have dependents, but excluding those with income levels between 40000 and 50000, what is the average priority score of those whose age is either below 35 or above 40, weighted by their income deviation from the group median income?

For citizens registered in January or March 2023 who either have no dependents with priority scores above 70, or have dependents with ages between 30-45 and income above 50000, calculate the total income of the subset where the priority score exceeds the overall average by at least 10 points, then divide by the count of citizens in this subset who are older than the median age of all qualifying citizens.

Identify citizens who registered in the first half of each month (days 1-15) and meet exactly one of these conditions: (income > 50000 AND has dependents) OR (age < 35 AND no dependents). Among these, find those whose priority score ranks in the top 30% of their respective registration month group, then calculate the ratio of their combined income to the total income of all citizens who have dependents but don't meet the initial filtering criteria.

title: Residence Permit and Household Registration Transfer Applications
questions: Among applications that are either Priority status with complete documents OR Standard status processed in Downtown office, but NOT both Priority AND Downtown simultaneously, what is the average processing time for Residence Permit applications that took longer than 30 days?

For applicants whose fee amount is above the median fee of all Priority status applications, but excluding those with incomplete documents in Rural offices, how many Household Transfer applications have processing times that exceed the average processing time of all Address Change applications?

If Priority status applications in Downtown offices had their processing times reduced by 20%, and we only consider applications with complete documents that cost more than 100, what would be the total processing time difference between the original and adjusted scenarios for applications that would still take more than 25 days after adjustment?
subdomain: Residence permit / Household registration transfer applications

title: Residence Permit Application Processing Records
questions: Among applications that are either Family_Reunion with complete documents OR Investment_Visa with expedited priority (but not both conditions simultaneously), and excluding any Work_Transfer applications processed in under 25 days, what is the average fee amount for applications that take more than the median processing time of their respective applicant type?

For applications where the priority status differs from the majority status within their applicant type, and the processing days exceed 40, calculate the total fee revenue from applications that have incomplete documents OR are Investment_Visa applications with processing times in the top 25% of all applications, but exclude any that satisfy both conditions?

Consider applications that are either expedited with incomplete documents OR standard priority with complete documents (but not applications that are expedited with complete documents). Among these, for applicant types where the average processing time exceeds 50 days, count how many applications have fee amounts that are above the overall median fee but below the maximum fee for their specific applicant type?
subdomain: Residence permit / Household registration transfer applications

title: Residence Permit Application Processing Records
questions: Among applications that are either Family_Reunion with complete documents OR Work_Transfer with expedited priority (but not both conditions simultaneously), calculate the average processing days for those with fees above 120, then identify how many applications in this filtered group have processing days within 10 days of this calculated average?

For applications where the applicant type is NOT Student_Registration AND either has incomplete documents OR processing days exceed 40, group by priority status and calculate the total fee revenue, then determine which priority group has the highest revenue but exclude any group where more than half the applications have processing days below 35?

Consider applications with complete documents where processing days are above the median for their respective applicant type, then among those that are either Premium priority OR have fees exactly 150, calculate the weighted average processing days (weighted by fee amount) and identify how many applications have processing days that exceed this weighted average by more than 15 days?
subdomain: Residence permit / Household registration transfer applications

title: Government Service Appointment Processing Log
questions: Among services that take longer than the median processing time of all Standard priority services, but shorter than the average processing time of High priority services with ratings above 3.5, what is the total fee amount for those services that either have ratings above 4.0 OR cost less than 200, but NOT both conditions simultaneously?

For services where the processing time exceeds 20 days AND the priority is High, calculate the weighted average rating using fee amounts as weights, then identify how many Standard priority services have ratings that exceed this weighted average while also having processing times that fall within the interquartile range of all service processing times?

If we exclude services with the top 3 highest fees and bottom 2 lowest ratings, then among the remaining services, what is the difference between the average processing time of services with above-median ratings versus below-median ratings, considering only those services where the fee per processing day ratio is either in the top 25% or bottom 25% of all calculated ratios?

title: Government Service Appointment Processing Log
questions: Among departments that have at least one Initial appointment with Priority_Score above 80 AND at least one Appeal case with Processing_Days over 15, which department has the highest average Priority_Score for services that are either (Renewal type with Bonus_Eligible='Yes') OR (Initial type with Processing_Days less than 12), excluding any Appeal cases from this calculation?

For services where the department has exactly 3 different appointment types represented, calculate the weighted priority score using the formula: (Initial appointments × 1.5) + (Renewal appointments × 1.2) + (Appeal appointments × 0.8). Then, among services in these qualifying departments, count how many have both Priority_Score above the department's weighted average AND Processing_Days below 15, but only if they are NOT Appeal type OR have Bonus_Eligible='Yes'?

Consider only departments where the ratio of Bonus_Eligible='Yes' services to total services is greater than 0.4. Within these departments, identify services that meet ALL of the following: Priority_Score is above the median for that specific department, Processing_Days is either in the bottom 25% OR the service is Initial type, and the appointment is NOT (Renewal type AND Bonus_Eligible='No'). What is the total Processing_Days for these qualifying services?

title: Government Service Appointment Logs
questions: Among departments that have at least one service requiring documentation AND have completed at least 2 services, what is the average satisfaction score for services that either cost more than $100 OR have high priority level, but exclude any service that takes less than 1.5 hours unless it has a satisfaction score above 4.0?

For services that are either pending or in-progress, calculate the total cost of services from departments where the average duration of completed services (within that department) exceeds 2.0 hours, but only include services that require documentation OR have medium/high priority, and exclude any service with satisfaction below 3.5?

What is the count of services that meet ALL of the following compound criteria: belong to a department with at least 3 different appointment types, have either no documentation requirement OR cost less than $75, are not low priority unless they have satisfaction above 4.2, and come from departments where the ratio of completed to total services is greater than 0.6?

title: Public Service Satisfaction Survey Results
questions: Among departments that have at least one service with a satisfaction score above 8.0 AND received performance bonuses, what is the average budget allocation for services that either have response counts below 200 OR satisfaction scores between 7.0 and 8.5 (exclusive of 8.5), but exclude any service where the response count exceeds 300 AND the satisfaction score is below 7.5?

For departments where the total budget allocation across all services exceeds 3 million, identify services that have satisfaction scores above the department's average satisfaction score AND either received no performance bonus OR have response counts in the bottom 25% of all services, then calculate the weighted average satisfaction score using response counts as weights for these filtered services?

Consider only services that belong to departments with exactly 2 service types listed. Among these, find services where the satisfaction score is above 7.5 OR the service received a performance bonus (but not both conditions simultaneously). For the remaining services, if we hypothetically increased all satisfaction scores by 0.5 points, how many services would then have satisfaction scores above 8.5 AND response counts above the median response count of the original filtered set?

title: Municipal Public Service Satisfaction Survey Results
questions: Among departments that received performance bonuses, what is the average satisfaction score for services that are either Critical budget category OR have more than 200 responses, but exclude any Non-Essential services that scored below 7.0?

For departments offering both Essential and Non-Essential services, calculate the weighted satisfaction difference where Essential services count double, then identify which department has the largest positive difference favoring Essential services?

If we redistribute bonuses such that only services with satisfaction scores above the median score of Critical budget services AND response counts in the top 40% qualify, how many currently bonus-receiving services would lose their bonus status?

title: Municipal Public Service Satisfaction Survey Results
questions: Among departments that have at least one service with a satisfaction score above 8.0 AND received performance bonuses, but excluding any department where ALL services have response counts below 300, what is the total budget allocation for services that scored between 7.0 and 8.5 (inclusive) but did NOT receive performance bonuses?

For departments where the average satisfaction score across all their services is above 7.0, identify those that have both bonus-eligible and non-bonus-eligible services, then calculate the weighted average satisfaction score (weighted by response count) for only the non-bonus-eligible services in these departments, but exclude any service with a budget below 1 million?

Among services that either have satisfaction scores in the top 25% OR response counts in the bottom 30%, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, and belong to departments with total budget allocations exceeding 4 million, how many of these services received performance bonuses while having satisfaction scores below the overall median satisfaction score?

title: Civil Aid Subsidy Applications
questions: Among applicants with household size greater than 3 who applied for either Housing or Food assistance, and whose monthly income is below 2500, what is the average subsidy amount for those with High priority status, excluding any applicant whose subsidy amount exceeds 900?

For applicants in the Medical or Education categories with Medium or High priority status, calculate the total subsidy amount for those whose income-to-household-size ratio is less than 700, but only include applicants whose subsidy amount is at least 50% of their calculated monthly per-person income threshold (monthly income divided by household size), then subtract the count of Low priority applicants in Housing category from this total.

Identify applicants who meet all of the following compound criteria: (1) either have High priority OR household size exceeds 4, (2) monthly income is between 1500-2800 OR application type is Food, (3) NOT in Education category unless priority is High, and (4) subsidy amount per household member exceeds 150. Among these filtered applicants, what is the difference between the highest and lowest monthly income values?

title: Civil Aid Subsidy Applications
questions: Among applicants who either have disability status OR apply for housing/medical programs (but not both conditions), and whose monthly income is below the median income of all applicants, what is the total application amount for those whose household size exceeds the average household size of applicants in the same income bracket?

For applicants whose income-to-household-size ratio is above the 75th percentile among non-disabled applicants, but whose application amount per household member is below the median of disabled applicants in utility or food programs, how many qualify if we exclude those whose total income would exceed 150% of poverty line (assuming $1500 per household member as poverty threshold)?

What is the average application amount for applicants who meet exactly two of these three criteria: (1) disability status is Yes, (2) household size is greater than the mode household size across all program types except Medical, and (3) their program type represents less than 25% of total applications, but only counting those whose income falls in the middle 50% range of their respective program type?

title: Civil Aid Subsidy Applications
questions: Among approved applicants with family sizes of 3 or more, what is the average subsidy amount for those whose monthly income is below the median income of all approved applicants, excluding any applicant whose subsidy amount per family member exceeds $150?

For applicants with monthly income between $2000-$3000 who are either approved with subsidy amounts above $400 OR pending with family sizes greater than 2, what is the total subsidy amount awarded to those whose income-to-family-size ratio is below the overall average ratio of all applicants in this filtered group?

Among all applicants whose monthly income exceeds $2500, identify those who are either rejected OR (approved but received less than $100 per family member in subsidy). For this subset, calculate the percentage of applicants whose family size is exactly 3, but only count applicants whose income is not the highest in their respective approval status group.

title: Tax Payment Records 2023
questions: Among taxpayers who either filed electronically with penalties applied OR filed on paper without penalties, what is the average tax owed by those earning more than $90,000 but excluding any taxpayer whose payment status is 'Paid' and whose income exceeds $140,000?

For taxpayers with partial payment status, calculate the total annual income of those who meet exactly one of these conditions: (penalty applied AND electronic filing) OR (no penalty AND paper filing), then subtract the count of taxpayers earning between $80,000-$120,000 who have unpaid status regardless of other factors.

What is the difference between the highest tax owed amount among electronic filers with penalties who are not fully paid, and the average tax owed by paper filers earning less than $100,000 who either have no penalty or have paid status but not both conditions simultaneously?

title: Corporate Tax Payment Records 2023
questions: Among businesses with annual revenue exceeding $2 million that either have penalties applied OR are in the Technology sector (but not both conditions simultaneously), what is the total tax liability for those with paid status, excluding any Manufacturing companies that have both penalties and overdue payments?

For taxpayers in non-Manufacturing sectors who have annual revenue between $1 million and $4 million, calculate the average effective tax amount for those without penalties, but only include businesses where the payment status is 'Paid' unless they are Technology companies with penalties applied, in which case include them regardless of payment status?

What is the difference in total annual revenue between two groups: (Group A) Retail and Services companies with no penalties that are either paid or have revenue below $1 million, versus (Group B) Manufacturing and Technology companies that have penalties applied but exclude any Technology companies with revenue above $4 million that are overdue?

title: Tax Payment Records 2023
questions: Among taxpayers who filed after March 15th and have either unpaid status OR partial payment status (but not both conditions simultaneously with penalty applied), what is the average annual income of those whose tax owed exceeds the median tax owed of all taxpayers with income above $100,000?

For taxpayers who filed in March, if we exclude those with penalties applied AND payment status of 'Paid', then among the remaining taxpayers, what is the total tax owed by those whose annual income is either below $90,000 OR above $150,000, but only if their payment status is not 'Unpaid'?

Consider taxpayers who either (have penalties applied AND income above $120,000) OR (filed after April 1st AND payment status is 'Partial'). Among this group, excluding those who filed in February, what is the count of taxpayers whose tax owed represents more than 20% of their annual income?

title: Government Employee Social Security Contributions
questions: Among employees in departments with average salaries above 4000, who are bonus eligible with contribution rates at least 0.11, but excluding those in Defense with more than 10 years of service, what is the total monthly contribution amount (salary × contribution rate) for the remaining qualified employees?

For employees with 5+ years of service who are either in Health with salaries below 4200 OR in Transportation with bonus eligibility, but not both conditions simultaneously, calculate the weighted average contribution rate where weights are determined by years of service divided by 10?

If the government implements a policy where employees in departments with fewer than 4 total employees get a 0.02 contribution rate increase, and bonus-eligible employees with salaries above the department median get an additional 0.01 increase, how many employees would have their final contribution rate exceed 0.13?

title: Government Employee Social Security Contributions
questions: Among departments where the average salary exceeds 4400 and at least 60% of employees are bonus eligible, what is the total monthly social security contribution for employees who have either more than 10 years of service OR are in the highest contribution rate tier, but exclude those who are both bonus eligible and have exactly between 8-12 years of service?

For employees in departments with contribution rates above 0.12, calculate the weighted average salary where weights are determined by years of service, but only include employees who are either not bonus eligible OR have salaries below the department median, then multiply by the count of departments that have more bonus-eligible than non-bonus-eligible employees?

What is the difference between the total contributions of bonus-eligible employees in high-contribution departments (rate > 0.15) versus the total contributions of non-bonus-eligible employees in all other departments, but only counting employees whose salary ranks in the top 3 within their respective department and have service years that are prime numbers?

title: Government Employee Social Security Contribution Details
questions: Among employees in Health and Education departments who are bonus eligible, have more than 5 years of service, and earn above the median salary of all bonus-eligible employees, what is the total monthly contribution amount (salary × contribution rate) for those whose contribution rate is either the highest or lowest within their respective departments?

For departments where the average salary of non-bonus-eligible employees exceeds 4000, calculate the difference between the highest and lowest monthly contributions among bonus-eligible employees in those departments, but only include employees whose years of service is greater than the department's average years of service and whose contribution rate is above 0.10?

Among employees whose salary is within 500 of their department's median salary, who are either bonus-eligible with less than 10 years of service OR non-bonus-eligible with more than 10 years of service, what is the average contribution rate for those whose monthly contribution amount ranks in the top 3 when compared to all employees meeting these initial criteria?

title: Government Information Disclosure Request Log
questions: Among departments that processed both Financial Records and Policy Documents requests, which department has the highest average fee for requests that took more than 10 days to process, excluding any requests marked as public interest unless the fee exceeds 100?

For requests that are either Budget Reports or Contract Details but not both types simultaneously, what is the total fee amount for departments that have an average processing time above 15 days when considering only non-public interest requests with fees greater than 150?

Which request type has the lowest median processing time when filtered to include only departments that processed at least 3 different request types, excluding any requests with zero fees unless they are from departments where the average fee across all their requests exceeds 120?

title: Government Information Disclosure Request Log
questions: Among departments that have at least one approved request with processing time exceeding 15 days, which department has the highest average fee amount for requests that are either approved with fees above $20 or pending with processing time below 20 days, excluding any records or budget requests?

For departments where the total fee revenue from approved requests exceeds $50, what is the processing time difference between the longest approved contract request and the shortest denied request of any type, but only considering departments that have processed both budget and policy requests?

If we exclude all requests with zero fees and all education department requests, then among the remaining departments, which one would rank second highest in terms of combined score calculated as: (number of approved requests × 10) + (average processing days × 2) - (number of denied requests × 5), but only for departments that have at least one request in each of the three non-zero fee categories (Records, Contracts, Policies)?

title: Government Information Disclosure Request Log
questions: Among departments that have at least one approved request with zero fees, what is the average processing time for their rejected requests that involve either Budget Info or Data Request types, excluding any department whose approved zero-fee requests took longer than 10 days to process?

For departments where the total fee amount from approved requests exceeds the total fee amount from rejected requests, calculate the difference between the maximum processing days of their approved requests and the minimum processing days of their rejected requests, but only consider departments that have processed both Document Access and Policy Records request types.

What is the total fee amount collected from approved requests in departments that have rejected at least two different request types, but only include fees from requests that took longer than the department's average processing time for approved requests, and exclude any department where more than half of their requests were rejected?

title: Administrative Penalty Notices Registry
questions: Among businesses that are either large-sized repeat offenders with unpaid environmental violations OR medium-sized non-repeat offenders with paid safety violations, but excluding any cases where the fine amount is below 10000 for large businesses or above 15000 for medium businesses, what is the total fine amount for the remaining qualifying cases?

For cases involving repeat offenders in either environmental or labor violations where the payment status differs from the majority payment pattern of their business size category, and excluding any small businesses with fines below 12000, calculate the average fine amount of the qualifying cases rounded to the nearest hundred?

Among all cases where the violation type is either tax or safety, identify those belonging to businesses that are either (large and non-repeat offenders) or (small and repeat offenders), then exclude any cases with unpaid status if their fine exceeds the median fine of their violation type category, and count how many cases remain?

title: Administrative Penalty Notices Database
questions: Among cases where the violation type is either Environmental or Safety but not both types appearing in paid status simultaneously, and excluding repeat offenders with fines above 10000, what is the total fine amount for unpaid cases that are overdue by more than 30 days?

For building and tax violations where payment status differs from the majority status within each violation type, and considering only cases where either the fine exceeds 7000 or the offender is a repeat violator but not both conditions together, what is the average fine amount?

Excluding cases that are both paid and have zero overdue days, among the remaining cases, if we group by repeat offender status and calculate the sum of fines for each group, then apply a penalty multiplier of 1.5 for repeat offenders and 1.2 for non-repeat offenders, what is the difference between the adjusted totals?

title: Administrative Penalty Notices 2024
questions: Among cases where the fine amount exceeds the average fine for Environmental violations, but excludes those with appeals filed, what is the total amount of unpaid or partial payments for cases that are overdue by more than 30 days?

For Safety violation cases that either have no appeal filed AND are overdue by more than 60 days, OR have an appeal filed but fine amount is below 15000, what is the average fine amount of those with unpaid status only?

What is the difference between the total fine amounts of Environmental cases with paid status versus the total of Tax cases that are either unpaid with more than 80 days overdue OR have partial payment status regardless of days overdue?

title: Policy Document Feedback Records
questions: Among policy documents with stakeholder support, what is the average budget allocation for those that either have a feedback score above 8.0 AND high priority, OR have a feedback score between 7.0-8.0 AND medium priority, but exclude any transportation policies with budget below 2 million?

For policy areas where at least 2 documents have high priority status, calculate the total budget of documents that have stakeholder support OR (feedback score > 8.5 AND medium/high priority), then subtract the budget of documents in the same areas that have no stakeholder support AND low priority. What is the final amount?

Identify policy documents that satisfy these compound conditions: (feedback score ≥ 8.0 AND stakeholder support) OR (budget > 2.5 million AND high priority), then among these, count how many belong to policy areas where the average feedback score of ALL documents in that area exceeds 7.5, but exclude any area where more than half the documents lack stakeholder support.

title: Policy Document Feedback Records
questions: Among departments that have at least one policy with a feedback score above 8.0 AND have policies in both 'Completed' and 'In Progress' status, which department has the highest average budget allocation for policies that are either 'Critical' priority with score above 7.5 OR 'High' priority with score above 8.0, excluding any suspended policies?

For policies where the implementation status is 'Completed' OR ('In Progress' AND budget > 3000000), calculate the weighted priority score where Critical=3, High=2, Medium=1, Low=0.5, then identify which department has the second-highest total weighted score when only considering policies with feedback scores in the top 60th percentile of all policies?

If we hypothetically change all 'Planning' status policies to 'In Progress' and increase their budgets by 15%, then among departments that would have exactly 3 or more 'In Progress' policies with scores ≥ 7.0, which department would show the largest percentage increase in total budget allocation compared to the current state, considering only policies with 'High' or 'Critical' priority?

title: Policy Document Feedback Records
questions: Among departments with at least 3 active policies, what is the average implementation cost of policies that have both public support and feedback scores above 8.0, excluding any department where the highest-scoring policy costs more than 350000?

For policies that are either under review with public support or active without public support, calculate the total implementation cost, then determine which department contributes the highest percentage to this total, but only considering departments that have exactly 2 policies in suspended or rejected status?

What is the difference between the average feedback score of policies costing less than 200000 in departments with public support rate above 60%, and the average feedback score of policies costing more than 300000 in departments where at least one policy is rejected, excluding any policy with status 'Suspended'?

title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment Report
questions: Among patients aged 50 or above who either have diabetes OR have both systolic blood pressure above 140 AND cholesterol above 200 (but not patients who satisfy all three conditions), what is the average heart risk score of those whose risk score is above the median risk score of the entire qualifying group?

For patients under 60 years old, if we exclude those with diabetes AND cholesterol below 200, then among the remaining patients, how many have a heart risk score that exceeds the average risk score of diabetic patients aged 60 or above with systolic blood pressure between 140-160?

Consider patients who are either (aged 40-65 with no diabetes) OR (aged above 65 with diabetes and systolic BP > 150). Within this group, exclude those whose cholesterol is in the bottom 25% of the group's cholesterol distribution. Among the remaining patients, what is the patient ID of the one with the highest heart risk score?

title: Patient Health Assessment Report
questions: Among patients who are either over 50 years old OR have diabetes (but not both conditions simultaneously), and whose systolic blood pressure exceeds 140 mmHg, what is the average cholesterol level for those who exercise less than 3 hours weekly, excluding any patient whose cholesterol is in the bottom 25th percentile of the entire dataset?

For patients who have diabetes AND are under 60 years old, but whose exercise hours are below the median exercise hours of non-diabetic patients over 40, calculate the total number of such patients whose systolic blood pressure is higher than the average systolic pressure of patients who exercise more than 4 hours weekly but do not have diabetes.

If we hypothetically reclassify patients as 'high-risk' when they have at least 2 of these 3 conditions: (age > 45, systolic BP > 150, cholesterol > 240), then among the newly classified high-risk patients who also have diabetes, what is the difference between the highest and lowest exercise hours weekly for those whose cholesterol exceeds the 75th percentile of all diabetic patients' cholesterol levels?

title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment Report
questions: Among patients aged 50 or above who either have diabetes OR have a cholesterol level exceeding 230 mg/dL (but not both conditions simultaneously), what is the average heart disease risk score for those whose systolic blood pressure is below 150 mmHg, excluding any patient whose risk score falls within the middle tercile of all patients in this filtered group?

For patients under 60 years old with no diabetes, calculate the weighted risk score using the formula: (Risk_Score × 0.6) + (Cholesterol_Level/100 × 0.4). Then, among those whose weighted score exceeds the median weighted score of this subgroup, how many have a systolic blood pressure that is either below 130 mmHg OR above 145 mmHg, but only if their original risk score is greater than 3.0?

Identify patients who satisfy exactly two of these three criteria: (1) age between 40-65, (2) cholesterol level above 200 mg/dL, (3) systolic blood pressure above 140 mmHg. Among this group, separate those with diabetes from those without, then calculate the difference between the highest risk score in the diabetes subgroup and the lowest risk score in the non-diabetes subgroup, but only consider patients whose risk scores are above the 75th percentile of their respective subgroups.

title: Hospital Reimbursement Performance Data
questions: Among hospitals that are either In-Network with Quality_Score above 8.0 OR Out-Network with Patient_Volume above 500, but excluding those that are both In-Network and have Reimbursement_Amount below 100000, what is the average Reimbursement_Amount for hospitals that are Bonus_Eligible and have Patient_Volume greater than the median Patient_Volume of all qualifying hospitals?

For hospitals where Network_Status is In-Network AND Quality_Score is above 7.5, create two groups: Group A (Bonus_Eligible = Yes AND Patient_Volume > 400) and Group B (Bonus_Eligible = No OR Patient_Volume ≤ 400). If we exclude hospitals from Group A that have Reimbursement_Amount in the top 25% of all In-Network hospitals, how many hospitals remain in the modified Group A, and what is their total Patient_Volume?

Consider hospitals that meet this compound criteria: (Quality_Score ≥ 8.0 AND Reimbursement_Amount > 120000) OR (Network_Status = Out-Network AND Bonus_Eligible = Yes). From this subset, exclude any hospital where Patient_Volume is below the 40th percentile of the entire dataset. Then, rank the remaining hospitals by a composite score calculated as (Quality_Score × 0.4 + Reimbursement_Amount/1000 × 0.3 + Patient_Volume/10 × 0.3). What is the Hospital_ID of the hospital with the 3rd highest composite score?

title: Hospital Reimbursement and Performance Data
questions: Among hospitals with quality scores above 85 that are either teaching hospitals with patient volumes exceeding 1400 OR non-teaching hospitals with specialty types other than General, what is the average reimbursement amount for those whose reimbursement per patient is below the median reimbursement per patient of all qualifying hospitals?

For hospitals that meet the criteria of being teaching institutions with quality scores between 80-90 (inclusive) OR being non-teaching cardiac/orthopedic specialty hospitals with patient volumes above 1000, calculate the total reimbursement amount for only those hospitals whose quality score ranks in the bottom 40% within their respective teaching status group, excluding any hospital with the highest patient volume in its specialty type.

Identify hospitals where the quality score is above the average quality score of all hospitals in their specialty type AND their reimbursement per patient exceeds 1800, then among these, find those that would still qualify if we hypothetically increased all quality score thresholds by 5 points while maintaining the same reimbursement per patient criterion, and calculate how many such hospitals have teaching status different from the majority teaching status of their specialty group.

title: Hospital Reimbursement and Performance Data
questions: Among hospitals that are either teaching institutions OR have emergency capabilities (but not both), and have a quality score above 85, what is the total reimbursement amount for those with patient volumes exceeding the median volume of all qualifying hospitals?

For non-teaching hospitals with emergency capabilities and quality scores between 88-95, calculate the weighted average reimbursement per patient (weight = quality score / 100), then identify how many teaching hospitals with emergency capabilities have a higher reimbursement per patient ratio than this weighted average?

If hospitals with quality scores below 80 lose their teaching status, and emergency-capable hospitals get a 15% reimbursement bonus, what would be the new total reimbursement for hospitals that would have both teaching status AND emergency capabilities under these new rules, excluding those with patient volumes in the bottom 25th percentile of the original dataset?

title: Patient Risk Assessment Records
questions: Among patients aged 50 or older with at least 3 chronic conditions, who have either high treatment compliance OR more than 5 emergency visits (but not both), what is the average insurance premium for those whose premium exceeds the median premium of all patients in this filtered group?

For patients under 40 years old with high treatment compliance, compare them against patients over 65 with low compliance: if we exclude patients with exactly 2 chronic conditions from both groups, what is the difference in total emergency visits between the remaining patients in these two age-compliance categories?

Among patients with medium treatment compliance, identify those whose emergency visits exceed twice their chronic conditions count, then from this subset, exclude patients whose insurance premium is below the average premium of all medium compliance patients - how many patients remain and what is their combined chronic conditions total?

title: Patient Medical Records Summary
questions: Among patients aged 50 or older with chronic conditions, what is the average treatment cost for those who either have Premium insurance but were NOT readmitted, or have Basic/Standard insurance AND were readmitted, excluding any Hypertension patients who have Premium coverage?

For patients under 60 years old, calculate the total treatment cost of those who meet ALL of the following criteria: have a chronic condition other than Asthma, were readmitted to the hospital, do NOT have Basic insurance coverage, and their treatment cost exceeds the median cost of all patients with the same chronic condition type.

What is the patient ID of the individual who has the highest treatment cost among patients who satisfy this complex condition: they are either (over 65 years old with Heart Disease and any readmission status) OR (under 40 years old with any chronic condition and Premium insurance), but they must NOT be Hypertension patients with Standard insurance coverage, and their cost must be above the average cost of all Premium insurance holders?

title: Patient Risk Assessment and Healthcare Utilization Summary
questions: Among patients who are either over 50 years old OR have more than 2 chronic conditions (but not both criteria simultaneously), and who also have a high-risk flag, what is the average insurance premium for those whose annual visits exceed the median visit count of all patients meeting the initial age/condition criteria?

For patients under 60 who have exactly 1 or 2 chronic conditions, calculate the total annual visits for those whose insurance premium is above the 75th percentile of premiums within their chronic condition group, but exclude any patient whose visit count is in the bottom quartile of all patients in the dataset.

Among high-risk patients whose age multiplied by chronic conditions exceeds 150, identify those whose insurance premium per visit ratio is below the average ratio of all patients with the same high-risk status, then determine how many of these patients would still qualify if we increased the age-condition threshold to 200.

title: Medication Prescription Records
questions: Among patients taking either Metformin or Atorvastatin with prescription durations of at least 60 days, but excluding those with insurance who have monthly costs below $50, what is the average daily dosage for the remaining patients?

For patients without insurance taking medications other than Lisinopril, if we only consider those whose daily dosage exceeds the median dosage of all patients in the dataset, how many of these patients have prescription durations that are exactly divisible by 30?

If we group patients by medication type and calculate the total monthly cost for each group, then exclude groups where more than half the patients have insurance, what is the difference between the highest and lowest total monthly costs among the remaining medication groups?

title: Medication Prescription Records
questions: Among patients with high-priority prescriptions who either have no insurance coverage OR report side effects (but not both conditions simultaneously), what is the total cost for medications with daily dosages above 25mg and prescription durations of at least 45 days, excluding any patient taking Metformin?

For patients whose total prescription cost exceeds $200 and who have insurance coverage, but excluding those with both medium priority AND side effects reported, what is the average daily dosage of medications that cost more than $5 per day, considering only prescriptions lasting more than 30 days?

Among patients taking medications costing less than $10 per day, who have either high priority prescriptions without side effects OR low priority prescriptions with insurance coverage (but not patients meeting both criteria), how many unique medications are prescribed for durations between 30-60 days inclusive, excluding patients with daily dosages below 20mg?

title: Medication Prescription Records
questions: Among patients prescribed medications for more than 45 days who either have insurance coverage OR are taking high-dosage medications (daily dosage > 50mg), but NOT both conditions simultaneously, what is the average cost per day for patients whose total prescription cost exceeds $75 and who are taking either Metformin or Atorvastatin?

For patients taking medications with duration between 30-60 days (inclusive), identify those whose cost per mg per day is below the median cost per mg per day of all patients in this duration range, then among these cost-efficient patients, count how many are taking cardiovascular medications (Lisinopril, Amlodipine, Metoprolol, Losartan) AND have insurance coverage, excluding any patient whose daily dosage is exactly divisible by 25?

Calculate the weighted average daily dosage for patients who meet ALL of the following criteria: (1) either have no insurance OR their total cost is above $60, (2) are NOT taking the lowest-cost medication in their respective dosage category (low: ≤25mg, medium: 26-75mg, high: >75mg), (3) their duration is either 30 days OR 90 days but not 45 or 60 days, where the weight is the ratio of their cost to the maximum cost among all qualifying patients?

title: Outpatient Emergency Registration Data
questions: Among patients who visited either Emergency or Cardiology departments, but not both types of departments if they had multiple visits, and who have premium insurance, what is the average wait time for those whose severity score is above the median severity score of all premium insurance patients in non-Neurology departments?

For patients who visited departments other than Emergency, if we exclude those with the lowest severity score in their respective department, and only consider those whose wait time exceeds the average wait time of Emergency patients with premium insurance, how many patients would qualify for a priority scheduling system that requires both non-premium insurance and a severity score that is either maximum in their department or at least 2 points above the department's minimum severity score?

If we create two groups - Group A: Emergency patients with severity scores above 7 and premium insurance, and Group B: non-Emergency patients with wait times above 100 minutes and severity scores below 6, then exclude any patients from both groups whose severity score equals the mode severity score across all departments, what is the difference between the total wait time of Group A and Group B?

title: Emergency Department Registration Data
questions: Among patients who either have Private insurance OR are over 60 years old (but not both conditions simultaneously), and whose emergency priority is not Low, what is the average treatment cost for those whose wait time exceeds the median wait time of all Medium priority patients?

For patients under 50 years old with either High priority OR Medicaid insurance (but excluding those who have both High priority AND Medicaid), calculate the total treatment cost, then determine how many patients over 65 with Medicare insurance have individual treatment costs that exceed 80% of this calculated total?

Among all patients whose age is between 30-60 (inclusive) and have either Private insurance or High priority (but not Low priority), identify those whose wait time is less than the average wait time of Uninsured patients, then count how many of these identified patients have treatment costs above the median cost of all Medium priority patients?

title: Outpatient Emergency Registration Data
questions: Among non-emergency patients with Premium insurance who either have priority scores above 8.0 OR wait times below 30 minutes (but not both conditions simultaneously), what is the average wait time for those whose registration type is Appointment, excluding any patient whose priority score is exactly between 7.5 and 8.5?

For patients who meet ALL of the following criteria: (Emergency_Flag is No AND Insurance_Coverage is not None) OR (Priority_Score > 8.0 AND Wait_Time_Minutes < 25), calculate the total priority score sum, but only include Walk-in patients if their wait time exceeds the average wait time of all Appointment patients, and exclude any patient whose priority score ranks in the top 3 highest among all patients?

If we hypothetically increase all priority scores by 1.0 for patients with Basic insurance AND decrease wait times by 10 minutes for Emergency patients, how many patients would then satisfy this compound condition: (Modified_Priority_Score > 8.5 AND Modified_Wait_Time < 20) OR (Registration_Type is Walk-in AND Insurance_Coverage is Premium AND original Wait_Time_Minutes was above 40), but exclude patients whose original Emergency_Flag was Yes unless their modified priority score exceeds 10.0?

title: Hospital Patient Expense and Outcome Records
questions: Among emergency patients who either had stays longer than 7 days OR total costs exceeding $20,000 (but not both conditions), and whose insurance coverage is above 0.85, what is the average out-of-pocket expense for those who were discharged home versus those transferred to another facility?

For elective patients with insurance coverage between 0.70 and 0.80 (inclusive), if we exclude those with the shortest and longest length of stay within this group, what would be the total insurance payout for the remaining patients, and how many of these remaining patients were discharged home?

Consider emergency patients whose total cost per day of stay exceeds $2,500. Among these, identify patients whose insurance coverage is either below 0.85 OR above 0.90 (but not between these values). What is the difference between the highest and lowest out-of-pocket expenses in this filtered group?

title: Hospital Patient Expense Records
questions: Among patients with emergency admissions who stayed longer than the average length of stay for their respective departments, and whose out-of-pocket costs exceed $15,000, what is the total insurance payout for Cardiology and Neurology patients combined, excluding those with insurance coverage below 0.7?

For departments where the average total cost of non-emergency patients exceeds $40,000, but only considering patients whose insurance coverage is either above 0.8 OR their length of stay is below 6 days (but not both conditions simultaneously), what is the maximum out-of-pocket expense among patients who stayed exactly at the median length of stay for their department?

If insurance coverage were increased by 0.1 for all patients with emergency admissions and total costs above $20,000, how many patients would then have out-of-pocket costs below $10,000, considering only those from departments where the current average insurance coverage for emergency patients is below 0.65?

title: Hospital Patient Expense and Risk Analysis
questions: Among patients with either Premium insurance or no insurance coverage, but excluding those in Emergency department, what is the average total cost for patients who stayed longer than 5 days AND have either High readmission risk OR are in Neurology department?

For departments where the average length of stay exceeds 5 days, calculate the total cost difference between patients with Basic insurance who have Medium or High readmission risk versus those with Premium insurance who have Low readmission risk, but only include patients whose individual costs are above the overall department average.

Among patients with readmission risk that is NOT Low, identify those in departments where at least 2 patients have Premium insurance, then from this subset, count how many patients have a cost-to-stay ratio (Total_Cost/Length_of_Stay) that exceeds the median cost-to-stay ratio of all Basic insurance patients with Medium readmission risk.

title: Medical Equipment Usage and Maintenance Log
questions: Among departments that have at least one piece of equipment with overdue maintenance status, what is the average usage hours for critical patient use equipment that are currently maintained, excluding any ventilators from the ICU department?

For equipment types that appear in exactly three different departments, calculate the total usage hours of devices that either have overdue maintenance OR are used for critical patients but not both, then determine which department contributes the highest usage hours to this total?

What is the combined usage hours of all non-critical patient use equipment in departments where the average usage hours of overdue maintenance equipment exceeds 250 hours, but only counting devices that are not MRI scanners and have current maintenance status?

title: Medical Equipment Usage and Maintenance Log
questions: Among equipment that either serves critical patients with usage hours above 200 OR has maintenance scores below 80 but is not in maintenance status, what is the average usage hours for active ventilators and dialysis machines combined, excluding any equipment with maintenance scores above 85?

For devices that are either critical patient equipment with maintenance scores between 75-90 OR non-critical equipment with usage hours above 180 but not both conditions simultaneously, how many active units have usage hours that exceed the average usage hours of all inactive equipment by more than 50 hours?

What is the total count of equipment units where the device type is either MRI_Scanner or CT_Scanner, the equipment serves critical patients only if usage hours are above 200, maintenance score is above 85 only if operational status is active, and the equipment must not be in maintenance status while having usage hours below 250?

title: Medical Equipment Usage and Maintenance Log
questions: Among departments that have at least two pieces of equipment with current maintenance status, which department has the highest average efficiency score for equipment that either has usage hours above 200 OR is a scanner type (MRI/CT) but not both conditions simultaneously?

What is the total usage hours for equipment that meets all of the following criteria: belongs to a department where the average efficiency score of overdue equipment is below 85, has current maintenance status, is not an Ultrasound, and has an efficiency score that exceeds the median efficiency score of all Current maintenance equipment?

If we were to redistribute overdue MRI Scanners and CT Scanners to departments that currently have no overdue equipment and an average efficiency score above 90, how many pieces of equipment would need to be moved, considering only departments that have at least 2 pieces of current equipment?

title: Patient Vaccination Records with Immunity Status
questions: Among patients who are either high-risk OR have received mRNA vaccines (but not both conditions simultaneously), and who have antibody levels below the median of their respective vaccine type group, what is the average number of doses received by those who are booster eligible and have been more than 180 days since their last dose?

For patients aged 50 and above who have received at least 2 doses, exclude those with mRNA vaccines if their antibody level exceeds 700, then among the remaining patients, calculate the total antibody level of those who are both high-risk and booster eligible, but only count patients whose days since last dose is within the top 40% range of all patients in this filtered group?

Consider patients who have either (high-risk status AND viral vector vaccine) OR (non-high-risk status AND mRNA vaccine with antibody level > 600). Among these, identify those whose dose count is above the average dose count of their age group (under 40, 40-65, over 65). For the qualifying patients, what is the difference between the highest and lowest antibody levels among those who are booster eligible but have fewer than 200 days since last dose?

title: Patient Vaccination Records
questions: Among patients who either received exactly 3 COVID-19 doses OR are high-risk Influenza patients (but not both conditions simultaneously), and excluding those who reported side effects, what is the average age of the remaining patients?

For patients aged 40 or above who have completed at least 2 doses of any vaccine, calculate the ratio of high-risk patients without side effects to non-high-risk patients with side effects, then multiply this ratio by the total number of COVID-19 patients in this filtered group.

Among all vaccine types, identify which vaccine has the highest proportion of patients who are either (high-risk AND have completed 3 doses) OR (non-high-risk AND reported side effects), then count how many patients of this vaccine type are aged between 30-60 and have completed fewer than 3 doses.

title: Patient Vaccination Records with Antibody Levels
questions: Among patients who received COVID-19 vaccines, what is the average antibody level for those who are either seniors with chronic conditions OR adults without chronic conditions who received at least 3 doses, but excluding any patient whose antibody level is below the median antibody level of all COVID-19 vaccinated patients?

For patients who received exactly 2 doses of any vaccine, calculate the weighted average antibody level where patients with chronic conditions have a weight of 1.5 and patients without chronic conditions have a weight of 1.0, but only include patients whose vaccine type appears in at least 3 different age groups in the dataset?

What is the difference in average antibody levels between two groups: Group A consists of patients who received the maximum number of doses for their specific vaccine type AND have chronic conditions, while Group B consists of patients who received fewer than the maximum doses for their vaccine type BUT have antibody levels above the 75th percentile of all patients in their age group?

title: Patient Health Survey Results
questions: Among patients aged 35-50 with chronic conditions who have mental health scores below the average of all patients with the same chronic condition, and whose physical activity hours exceed the median for their age group, what is the total insurance premium for those whose premium is above the 75th percentile of all patients in their chronic condition category?

For patients who either have no chronic condition with mental health scores above 80 OR have diabetes with physical activity hours below 6, but excluding those whose age is in the bottom quartile of their respective chronic condition group, what is the average mental health score of those whose insurance premium ranks in the top 3 within their filtered subset?

Among patients whose mental health score is above the mean for their chronic condition group AND whose physical activity hours place them in the top 50% of all patients, but excluding those whose insurance premium is below the median of patients with the same chronic condition, how many patients have an age that is within 5 years of the average age of patients who meet all the same criteria except for the insurance premium exclusion?

title: Mental Health Survey Results
questions: Among patients who either have insurance and are over 40 years old, or have no insurance but a BMI under 25, what is the average mental health score for those who also have fewer than 3 chronic conditions but exclude any patient whose mental health score is above 85 unless they have exactly 1 chronic condition?

For patients aged 50 or above who have insurance, calculate the total chronic conditions count, but only include those whose BMI is either below 26 or above 30, and whose mental health score is below the overall average mental health score of uninsured patients under 45 years old with zero chronic conditions?

What is the difference between the highest BMI among patients who have 2 or more chronic conditions and are either uninsured with mental health scores above 70, or insured with mental health scores below 75, versus the lowest BMI among patients who have fewer than 2 chronic conditions and are either under 35 years old with insurance, or over 60 years old without insurance?

title: Mental Health Treatment Survey Results
questions: Among patients who either have premium insurance with BMI above 25 OR have basic insurance with depression scores above 15, but excluding those who receive combined treatment and have chronic conditions, what is the average anxiety score of those who require follow-up?

For patients aged 30-45 who don't have chronic conditions, compare the count of those receiving therapy with depression scores below 10 versus those receiving medication with anxiety scores above 15, but only include patients whose BMI classification (normal: <25, overweight: ≥25) matches their insurance type preference (premium for normal, basic for overweight), then determine which group has more patients?

What is the total depression score sum for patients who meet all of the following compound criteria: either (age above 40 AND premium insurance) or (BMI above 28 AND basic insurance), but not both conditions simultaneously, AND they either require follow-up without chronic conditions OR have chronic conditions without requiring follow-up?

title: Telemedicine Consultation Records
questions: Among patients who had consultations longer than 40 minutes OR had a symptom severity score of 8 or higher, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, and who either received a prescription without follow-up being required OR had follow-up required without receiving a prescription, what is the average patient satisfaction rating for those whose satisfaction rating is above the overall median satisfaction rating of all patients in the dataset?

For patients whose consultation duration is above the average duration of all patients who received prescriptions, and whose symptom severity score is either in the top 25% of all scores OR exactly equals the mode of severity scores among patients without follow-up requirements, but excluding those who have both high satisfaction (above 4.5) AND low severity (below 6), what is the total number of such patients who also have consultation durations that are prime numbers?

Consider patients who satisfy exactly two of these three conditions: (1) consultation duration exceeds 35 minutes, (2) symptom severity score is 7 or above, (3) patient satisfaction rating is below 4.2. Among these patients, identify those who either received a prescription AND required follow-up, OR received neither prescription nor follow-up. For the remaining subset after applying an additional filter to exclude patients whose duration is a multiple of 10, what is the sum of their symptom severity scores divided by the count of patients in this final group, rounded to one decimal place?

title: Telemedicine Consultation Records
questions: Among patients who had consultations lasting more than 30 minutes OR required follow-up, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, and whose satisfaction score is above the average satisfaction score of Emergency consultations, what is the total cost for those who had either Specialist or Mental_Health consultations but exclude any General consultations that cost more than $75?

For patients whose consultation duration is above the median duration of their respective consultation type AND who either have a satisfaction score in the top 25% of all patients OR require follow-up (but not patients who satisfy both conditions), calculate the average cost difference between those who had Specialist consultations versus those who had Mental_Health consultations, excluding any Emergency consultations?

Among patients who require follow-up, identify those whose satisfaction score is either below the average of General consultations OR above the average of Specialist consultations (but not those meeting both criteria), then among this subset, count how many had consultation durations that exceed the 75th percentile of Emergency consultation durations while having costs that fall between the minimum and maximum costs of Mental_Health consultations?

title: Telemedicine Consultation Records
questions: Among patients who require follow-up and have either Cardiology or Neurology consultations, but exclude those with insurance coverage below 80%, what is the average satisfaction score for patients whose consultation duration exceeds the median duration of all qualifying patients?

For specialists where the average satisfaction score of patients requiring follow-up is higher than those not requiring follow-up, calculate the total consultation minutes for patients with insurance coverage above 85% but satisfaction scores below the specialty's overall average, excluding any consultation shorter than 35 minutes.

Compare the weighted satisfaction scores (satisfaction × insurance coverage percentage) between two groups: Group A consists of Cardiology and Psychiatry patients with follow-up required and duration ≥ 40 minutes; Group B consists of Dermatology and Neurology patients without follow-up and satisfaction ≥ 8.0. What is the difference in average weighted scores between these groups?

title: Employee Onboarding Performance Data
questions: Among employees who either work in Engineering with certification requirements OR work in Sales without certification requirements, and who are also bonus eligible, what is the average training score of those whose onboarding took longer than the median onboarding days of all Marketing employees who scored above 80?

For departments where at least 2 employees are both bonus eligible and have training scores above 85, but excluding any department where more than half of its employees require certification, what is the total number of onboarding days for employees who are not bonus eligible but have training scores in the top 25% of all employees?

If we create two groups: Group A contains employees from departments with average training scores below 82 who are bonus eligible, and Group B contains employees from departments with average training scores of 82 or above who require certification, what is the difference between the maximum onboarding days in Group A and the minimum training score in Group B?

title: Employee Onboarding Progress Tracker
questions: Among employees who either have mentorship assigned OR are bonus eligible (but not both), and whose training score is above the average of all employees in their respective departments, what is the total number of days to complete onboarding for those in Engineering or Sales departments only?

For departments where the average training score of bonus-eligible employees exceeds 87, calculate the weighted average days to complete (weighted by training score) for employees who have mentorship assigned but are NOT bonus eligible, excluding any employee whose days to complete is in the top 25% of all employees?

If we implement a new policy where employees with training scores below 85 AND no mentorship become bonus eligible, while employees with scores above 90 AND mentorship lose bonus eligibility, how many employees in Marketing and Finance departments combined would have their bonus eligibility status changed from the original data?

title: Employee Onboarding Performance Data
questions: Among employees with active certifications who scored above 85 in training, calculate the average years of experience for those in technical departments (Engineering/Finance) who are bonus eligible, but exclude any employee whose training score is exactly divisible by 3 and whose years of experience is less than 5?

What is the total number of employees who either have pending certifications with training scores between 80-90 OR have expired certifications with more than 4 years experience, but only count those from non-sales departments who would become bonus eligible if we changed the policy to include all employees with training scores above 82?

If we rank departments by the weighted average of (Training_Score × 0.6 + Years_Experience × 10 × 0.4) for employees with active certifications, but exclude any employee who is both bonus eligible and has less than 5 years experience, what is the ranking position of the Marketing department?

title: Employee Performance and Compensation Directory
questions: Among departments where the average performance score of bonus-eligible employees exceeds 8.0, and where at least 3 employees have more than 4 years of experience, what is the total salary cost for employees who either have a performance score above 8.5 OR have more than 6 years of experience (but not both conditions simultaneously)?

For employees in departments that have both: (1) at least one employee with performance score above 9.0 AND (2) at least two non-bonus-eligible employees, calculate the average salary of those employees who have performance scores between 7.0 and 8.5 (inclusive) and are bonus-eligible, then identify which department has employees closest to this calculated average salary?

If we exclude departments where more than 50% of employees are not bonus-eligible, and among the remaining departments, consider only employees who have either (performance score > 8.0 AND years of experience ≤ 5) OR (performance score ≤ 7.5 AND years of experience > 5), what is the difference between the highest and lowest individual salaries in this filtered group?

title: Employee Performance and Compensation Directory
questions: Among departments where the average performance score of bonus-eligible employees exceeds 8.0, and excluding any department where non-bonus-eligible employees have an average salary above 70000, what is the total salary of employees who have either more than 5 years experience OR a performance score above 8.5 (but not both conditions simultaneously)?
