For employees in departments that have at least 3 bonus-eligible staff members, calculate the weighted average salary where the weight is the performance score, but only include employees who satisfy exactly one of these conditions: (years of experience > 4) OR (performance score > 8.0), then identify which department has the highest such weighted average?

Consider only departments where the ratio of bonus-eligible to total employees is greater than 0.5, then among employees in these departments who have performance scores in the top 50% within their respective departments, count how many have salaries that fall below the overall median salary of all bonus-eligible employees across the entire company?

title: Research Study Annotation Results
questions: Among studies that are either peer-reviewed Clinical studies with sample sizes above 200 OR non-peer-reviewed Experimental studies with funding above 150000, but excluding any study with accuracy below 85, what is the average funding amount for those remaining studies that also have accuracy scores in the top 30% of this filtered subset?

For studies where the research type is NOT Meta-Analysis, calculate the total sample size of peer-reviewed studies with accuracy above 90, then subtract the total sample size of non-peer-reviewed studies with funding below 100000 and accuracy above 85, but only count studies where sample size exceeds 250 in both calculations.

If we create two groups - Group A: Clinical or Observational studies with peer review status matching their funding tier (high funding >120000 gets peer review, low funding ≤120000 gets no peer review), and Group B: Experimental studies with accuracy above the median accuracy of all Experimental studies - what is the difference between the highest accuracy score in Group A versus Group B?

title: Chemical Compound Environmental Impact Study
questions: Among compounds that are either biodegradable with toxicity score below 4.0 OR non-biodegradable with solubility above 200 mg/L (but not both conditions), and tested at temperatures between 20-35°C inclusive, what is the average pH level of those compounds that also have a toxicity score that is either the minimum or maximum within this filtered subset?

For compounds tested at temperatures above 25°C that are biodegradable, calculate the weighted environmental safety score using the formula: (10 - toxicity_score) × (solubility/100) × pH_factor, where pH_factor is 1.2 if pH > 7.0, otherwise 0.8. Then exclude any compound whose weighted score is not within the top 3 or bottom 2 of this calculated group. What is the sum of solubility values for the remaining compounds?

Consider compounds that satisfy exactly two of these three criteria: (1) solubility > 300 mg/L, (2) toxicity score < 5.0, (3) pH level > 7.0. Among these, group by biodegradability status and temperature ranges (20-30°C vs 31-45°C). For the group combination with the highest average toxicity score, but only including compounds whose solubility rank within that group is either 1st or last, what is the total count of such compounds?

title: Multi-Variable Chemical Treatment Experiment Results
questions: Among experiments using Chemical_A or Chemical_B but not Chemical_C, conducted at temperatures above 30°C, with pressure conditions either below 100 kPa or above 108 kPa, what is the average yield percentage for those experiments that also have a quality score greater than 8.0?

For experiments where the treatment type is Chemical_B and the temperature is at least 35°C, or where the treatment type is Chemical_A with pressure above 105 kPa, but excluding any experiments with yield below 80%, what is the total number of experiments that have quality scores in the top 25% of all recorded quality scores?

If we rank all Chemical_A experiments by a composite score calculated as (Yield_Percent × 0.6 + Quality_Score × 10 × 0.4), then filter for those conducted at temperatures between 25-35°C inclusive with pressure not equal to 101.3 kPa, and finally exclude any with yields below the median yield of all Chemical_A experiments, what is the experiment ID of the highest-ranked remaining experiment?

title: Multi-Treatment Growth Rate Experiment Results
questions: Among experiments with temperatures above 27°C that either used Chemical_A or Chemical_B (but not both in the same comparison), and excluding any experiments where pH is below 6.7 or above 7.3, what is the average growth rate of successful experiments, weighted by the temperature deviation from 29°C (where experiments closer to 29°C get higher weight)?

For experiments that succeeded with non-control treatments, group them by treatment type, then for each group calculate the median growth rate, but only include groups where at least 2 experiments had pH levels between 6.8 and 7.2 inclusive, and the group's maximum temperature exceeds 28°C. What is the difference between the highest and lowest median growth rates among qualifying groups?

Consider experiments where the growth rate exceeds the overall average growth rate of successful experiments by at least 2 mm/day, but exclude any experiment where either the temperature is in the bottom 25th percentile or the pH deviates more than 0.3 from 7.0. Among the remaining experiments, count how many used Chemical_B, then simulate what would happen if we reclassified all Chemical_C experiments in this subset as Chemical_B - what would be the new total count of Chemical_B experiments in this filtered subset?

title: Research Project Progress Reports
questions: Among projects that are either in Phase_2 with external funding OR in Phase_3 without external funding, but NOT projects that have both high risk and completion rate below 70%, what is the average budget of those remaining projects that also have a completion rate above the median completion rate of all Phase_1 projects?

For projects where the risk level is 'Medium' AND (budget is above 200000 OR completion rate is above 80%), exclude any project that simultaneously has external funding equal to 'Yes' and is in Phase_3, then calculate the total budget of the remaining projects, but only count those whose completion rate ranks in the top 50% within their respective research phase?

Consider projects that satisfy exactly one of these conditions: (Risk_Level is 'Low' AND Budget > 150000) OR (Has_External_Funding is 'No' AND Completion_Rate > 85). Among these filtered projects, group them by research phase and find the phase with the highest average completion rate, but exclude any phase where more than 60% of its projects have budgets below 200000?

title: Research Project Progress Report Q3 2024
questions: Among projects with budgets exceeding $200,000, what is the average progress score of those that either have milestone bonuses AND belong to Chemistry category, OR have progress scores above 85 but do NOT have milestone bonuses and are NOT in the Physics category?

If we exclude all Biomedical projects with budgets below $200,000, and then consider only the remaining projects that have milestone bonuses OR progress scores above 90, what is the total budget allocation for projects where the principal investigator's name contains either 'Dr. M' or 'Dr. T' but the project is NOT in the Chemistry category?

Among projects that satisfy ALL of the following: (budget between $180,000-$280,000 AND progress score below 90) OR (budget above $280,000 AND has milestone bonus), how many projects belong to categories other than Physics, and what is the difference between the highest and lowest progress scores within this filtered group?

title: Research Project Progress Report Q3 2024
questions: Among projects that are either in Experimentation phase with external funding OR in Analysis phase without external funding, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, what is the average budget of those projects that have completion rates below 50% and are classified as High priority?

For projects where the priority level is High AND the completion rate is above 70%, OR projects where the priority level is Medium AND they have external funding AND completion rate is below 60%, calculate the total budget difference between externally funded and non-externally funded projects within this filtered set, then determine how many projects would need to be excluded if we removed the lowest budget project from each research phase represented?

If we create two groups: Group A contains High priority projects in either Data Collection or Experimentation phases with completion rates above 75%, and Group B contains Medium priority projects with external funding in either Analysis or Literature Review phases with budgets below 100000, what would be the weighted average completion rate of the combined groups, where Group A projects are weighted by 2.5 and Group B projects are weighted by 1.5, and how many projects total contribute to this calculation?

title: Public Transit Card Usage Records
questions: Among cards that used peak hours services and have more than 35 trips, what is the average fare per trip for those using Bus routes but excluding cards with student discounts, compared to those using Metro routes with student discounts?

For cards that either have student discounts OR use peak hours (but not both), and have made between 25-50 trips, what is the total fare collected from Metro routes, excluding Metro_C users who have fewer than 30 trips?

If we rank all cards by their fare-per-trip ratio in descending order, but only consider cards that use peak hours AND either have student discounts or made more than 40 trips, what is the Card_ID of the card that would rank 3rd after excluding any Bus_7 users with total fare less than 50?

title: Public Transit Card Swipe Records
questions: Among cards that used either Bus or Tram routes (but not Metro), and had trip durations exceeding 30 minutes during peak hours OR traveled more than 10 km during non-peak hours, what is the average fare amount for those cards whose distance-to-duration ratio is greater than 0.35 km per minute?

For cards that used Metro during peak hours with fares above $4.00, or used Bus during non-peak hours with distances below 10 km, exclude any cards where the fare per kilometer exceeds $0.40. Among the remaining cards, how many had trip durations that fall within the middle 50% range when all qualifying cards are sorted by duration?

Consider cards that either (traveled more than 15 km on Metro during any time) OR (used Bus/Tram during peak hours with duration over 25 minutes). From this group, exclude cards where fare amount is exactly proportional to distance (fare/distance ratio between 0.25-0.35). For the remaining cards, what is the total fare amount for those whose trip efficiency (distance/duration) ranks in the top 3 positions?

title: Public Transit Card Swipe Records
questions: Among stations that have both Student and Senior card swipes during peak hours, and where the average transaction amount for Regular cards at those same stations exceeds 3.25, what is the total transaction amount for all non-Regular card types at these qualifying stations during non-peak hours only?

For card types that appear at exactly 3 different stations, calculate the weighted average transaction amount where peak hour transactions have double weight compared to non-peak transactions, then identify how many stations have at least one swipe from these card types with a transaction amount above this weighted average during peak hours?

Consider stations where the difference between the highest and lowest transaction amounts is greater than 1.00, and among these stations, find those that have swipes from all three card types but where Senior card holders never paid the maximum transaction amount at that station. What is the sum of all Student card transaction amounts at these qualifying stations?

title: Taxi Order Information
questions: Among trips that either occurred during peak hours with Premium customers OR were Corporate trips with distances exceeding 15 miles (but not both conditions simultaneously), and excluding any trips with driver ratings below 4.0 or fare amounts under $25, what is the average trip distance for the remaining qualifying orders?

For orders where the customer type is Premium and the trip distance is above the median distance of all Corporate trips, but only if the driver rating is at least 4.5 AND the trip did not occur during peak hours, calculate the total fare amount and determine how many such orders exist, then provide the ratio of total fare to order count?

If we hypothetically increased all non-peak hour fares by 15% and decreased all peak hour fares by 8%, then among trips with ratings between 4.0 and 4.5 (inclusive) that are either Regular customer trips over 10 miles OR Corporate trips under 20 miles (excluding Premium customers entirely), what would be the weighted average fare per mile, where the weight is the original driver rating?

title: Taxi Order Information Dataset
questions: Among trips that are either during peak hours with rating above 4.0 OR non-peak hours with distance greater than 15km, but excluding those paid by cash during peak hours, what is the average fare amount for the remaining orders that also have a rating-to-distance ratio greater than 0.25?

For drivers with ratings between 3.5 and 4.5 (inclusive), if we group them by payment method and only consider groups where the total distance exceeds 40km, then within each qualifying group, count only trips where fare per kilometer is above the group's median fare per kilometer - what is the total count across all qualifying groups?

If we apply a bonus system where trips get a bonus only if they satisfy: (peak hours AND rating ≥ 4.2) OR (non-peak hours AND distance > 12km AND digital payment), then among bonus-eligible trips, exclude those where fare amount is in the bottom 25% of all bonus-eligible fares, what is the sum of trip distances for the remaining high-value bonus trips?

title: Taxi Order Information
questions: Among orders with surge pricing active and driver ratings above 4.0, calculate the average fare amount for credit card payments, then identify how many cash payment orders (regardless of surge status) have fare amounts exceeding this calculated average but only if their trip distance is less than 6 miles and driver rating is at least 4.2?

For orders where either surge is active OR payment method is credit (but not both conditions simultaneously), filter those with driver ratings between 4.0 and 4.5 inclusive, then among the remaining orders, what is the total fare amount for trips longer than 4 miles, excluding any order where the fare per mile ratio exceeds 5.2?

Starting with orders that have no surge pricing, group them by payment method, calculate the median trip distance for each group, then count how many surge-active orders have driver ratings above 4.3 AND trip distances that fall within 0.5 miles of either calculated median, but only if their fare amount is in the top 40% of all surge-active orders?

title: Subway Station Passenger Flow and Operational Data
questions: Among Express line stations with transfer capabilities, what is the total peak hour passenger flow for those stations that have either a maintenance score above 85 OR a combined peak and off-peak flow exceeding 15000, but excluding any station where the off-peak flow represents more than 40% of the peak flow?

For Local line stations without transfer capabilities, calculate the average maintenance score of stations that have peak hour flow between 4000-6000 passengers AND off-peak flow less than 2500, then identify how many Express stations with transfers have maintenance scores higher than this calculated average while also having peak flows that exceed the median peak flow of all qualifying Local stations?

What is the difference in total combined passenger flow (peak + off-peak) between the group of stations that are either Express with no transfers OR Local with transfers, compared to stations that have maintenance scores in the 80-90 range AND peak flows above 7000, excluding any station where the maintenance score is exactly 85 or the off-peak flow is below 3000?

title: Subway Station Passenger Flow Statistics
questions: Among stations with transfer capabilities and accessibility scores above 80, calculate the average peak-hour flow for Express stations, then identify how many Local stations in this filtered group have peak-hour flows that exceed this calculated average by more than 5000 passengers?

For stations where the off-peak flow represents more than 35% of peak-hour flow, exclude those with accessibility scores below 75, then among the remaining Express stations without transfer capabilities, what is the total combined passenger flow (peak + off-peak) of the station with the highest accessibility score?

Create two groups: Group A contains Local stations with transfers and accessibility scores ≥ 85, Group B contains Express stations without transfers but with peak flows > 30000. Calculate the difference between Group A's average off-peak flow and Group B's average off-peak flow, then determine how many stations in Group B have individual off-peak flows that fall below this calculated difference value?

title: Metropolitan Subway Passenger Flow Statistics
questions: Among stations that have express service AND are on either Red or Blue lines, which station has the highest combined passenger flow (peak + off-peak), but only if its accessibility rating is above 4.0 AND its off-peak passengers exceed 2000, excluding any station where peak hour passengers are less than 6000?

What is the total peak hour passenger count for stations that meet ALL of the following criteria: (1) accessibility rating between 3.5 and 4.5 (inclusive), (2) either on Green line without express service OR on Yellow line with more than 5000 peak passengers, (3) off-peak passengers less than 2200, AND (4) not having the word 'Center' or 'Plaza' in their name?

If we create two groups - Group A: Red/Blue line stations with express service and accessibility rating > 4.2, and Group B: Green/Yellow line stations with no express service and peak passengers > 4000 - what is the difference between Group A's average off-peak passengers and Group B's average off-peak passengers, rounded to the nearest whole number?

title: Urban Parking Zone Records
questions: Among parking zones with electric charging that have occupancy rates above 0.70 and maintenance scores below 9.0, calculate the average monthly fee for those zones where the peak hours surcharge is either above 20 or the zone name contains 'Downtown', but exclude any zone where both the monthly fee exceeds 170 and the occupancy rate is above 0.90.

For zones without electric charging where the maintenance score is above 7.0, identify which zone has the highest combined score calculated as: (Occupancy_Rate × 100) + (Maintenance_Score × 5) - (Peak_Hours_Surcharge ÷ 2), but only consider zones where the monthly fee is below the median monthly fee of all non-electric zones, and the zone type (first word before underscore) appears at least twice in the dataset.

Compare the total revenue potential (Monthly_Fee × Occupancy_Rate × 100 spaces assumed per zone) between two groups: Group A consists of electric charging zones with maintenance scores above 8.0 and peak surcharges below 30, versus Group B consisting of non-electric zones where either the occupancy rate exceeds 0.75 or the maintenance score is above 8.5, but exclude from both groups any zone where the monthly fee is in the bottom 25% of all zones. What is the difference in total revenue potential between these groups?

title: Urban Parking Zone Performance Records
questions: Among zones where the daily rate is above the median rate for premium locations but the occupancy rate is below 90%, and excluding zones with violation counts in the top 25% of all zones, what is the total monthly revenue of the remaining zones that have either the highest or lowest daily rate within this filtered subset?

For non-premium zones with occupancy rates above 85%, if we were to redistribute violation counts by giving each zone the average violation count of premium zones with similar occupancy ranges (within 5 percentage points), which zone would experience the largest absolute change in violation count, and what would be the new violation count?

Consider zones where monthly revenue per unit occupancy rate exceeds 180, but only if they are either premium locations with violation counts below 40 or non-premium locations with violation counts above 15. Among these qualifying zones, rank them by a composite score calculated as (occupancy_rate × 0.4) + (daily_rate × 0.3) + ((100 - violation_count) × 0.3), and identify the zone with the median composite score.

title: Urban Parking Zone Performance Data
questions: Among parking zones with premium service that have either occupancy rates above 0.80 OR daily rates below $20 (but not both conditions), and excluding any zone with a revenue score below 6.0, what is the average monthly pass price for zones that also have occupancy rates at least 0.10 higher than the median occupancy rate of all non-premium zones?

For zones located in areas containing 'town' in their name, if we group them by whether they offer premium service, and then within each group rank them by a composite score calculated as (Daily_Rate × 0.4 + Revenue_Score × 10), what is the total monthly pass revenue potential of the top 2 zones from the premium group minus the top 2 zones from the non-premium group?

Consider zones that have occupancy rates within the top 25% of all zones AND either have premium service with daily rates exceeding $25 OR lack premium service but have revenue scores above 8.0. If we exclude zones where the ratio of monthly pass to daily rate is less than 15, how many zones remain that also have names starting with letters from the second half of the alphabet (N-Z)?

title: Highway Toll Records
questions: Among vehicles that traveled during peak hours OR are frequent users (but not both), and have toll amounts exceeding the average toll of all cars, what is the total distance traveled by trucks that also have distances greater than 35 miles?

For vehicles where the toll amount per mile is below 0.55 AND either they are frequent users traveling during non-peak hours OR they are non-frequent users traveling during peak hours, what is the average toll amount of cars that have distances between 20-30 miles inclusive?

Among trucks that either traveled more than 40 miles during peak hours OR paid more than $20 during non-peak hours, but excluding those that are both frequent users and have toll-per-mile ratios above 0.50, how many vehicles have toll amounts that exceed the median toll amount of all frequent user cars?

title: Highway Toll Payment Records
questions: Among commercial vehicles that traveled during peak hours on either B2-East or C3-West sections, but excluding those that paid more than $25 or traveled less than 35 miles, what is the average toll amount for the remaining vehicles?

For non-commercial vehicles on A1-North or D4-South sections during non-peak hours, if we apply a hypothetical 15% surcharge to those traveling more than 20 miles but exclude any resulting toll above $15, how many vehicles would have their toll amount modified and what would be their total combined toll after the surcharge?

Compare the toll revenue per mile ratio between two groups: Group A consists of peak-hour commercial vehicles on C3-West with distances above the median distance of all C3-West vehicles, and Group B consists of non-peak commercial vehicles on B2-East with toll amounts below the average toll of all B2-East vehicles. Which group has the higher average toll-per-mile ratio?

title: Highway Toll Transaction Records
questions: Among vehicles that traveled during peak hours and are either Cars with discount eligibility OR Trucks without discount eligibility, what is the average toll amount for those whose distance exceeds the median distance of all SUVs in the dataset?

For vehicles that are NOT Cars, calculate the total toll revenue from those that either (traveled during peak hours AND are discount eligible) OR (traveled during non-peak hours AND have toll amounts above the average toll of all Cars), then determine how many such qualifying vehicles have distances within 5 miles of the overall dataset average distance?

If discount eligible vehicles during peak hours had their toll reduced by 15%, and non-peak Trucks had their toll increased by 10%, what would be the difference between the highest and lowest adjusted toll amounts among vehicles whose original distance was between the 25th and 75th percentile of all vehicle distances?

title: Daily Flight Operations Report
questions: Among flights with Boeing 737 aircraft that either have premium service OR carry more than 160 passengers (but not both conditions), and excluding any flights with delays exceeding 20 minutes, what is the average fuel efficiency score of the remaining flights?

For flights that have premium service AND fuel efficiency scores above 7.5, but excluding Boeing 777 aircraft, calculate the total passenger count, then determine how many Airbus A320 flights in the entire dataset have passenger counts below this calculated threshold?

Consider flights with delays between 10-30 minutes (inclusive) that do NOT have premium service. Among these, identify those with fuel efficiency scores in the top 50% within this subset, then count how many Boeing aircraft types (737 or 777) appear in this final filtered group?

title: Daily Flight Operations Report
questions: Among flights that either depart from New York OR arrive in Los Angeles (but not flights that both depart from New York AND arrive in Los Angeles), and have passenger counts above the average passenger count of all on-time flights, what is the total cargo weight of those flights that were delayed?

For airlines with at least 3 flights in the dataset, calculate the average passenger count of their delayed flights only, then identify which airline has the highest such average, and determine how many of that airline's on-time flights have cargo weight exceeding 2000 KG?

Consider flights departing from cities that also serve as arrival destinations for at least 2 other flights in the dataset. Among these flights, exclude any that have both passenger count below 150 AND cargo weight below 2000 KG. Of the remaining flights, what is the difference between the maximum and minimum passenger counts of delayed flights only?

title: Flight Operations and Passenger Manifest Data
questions: Among flights that are either Boeing 777s with more than 280 passengers OR Airbus A380s with cargo weight below 12000kg, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, calculate the average passenger count for those that also have on-time performance of 'Yes' and are international routes, then subtract the count of domestic Boeing 737s with passenger count above 130 and poor on-time performance?

For aircraft types that have at least 2 flights with on-time performance 'Yes' AND at least 1 flight with cargo weight exceeding 8000kg, identify which specific aircraft type has the highest ratio of total passengers to total cargo weight when considering only their international flights with passenger counts between 150-350, excluding any flights where cargo weight is exactly divisible by 1000?

If we group flights by route type, then within each group exclude flights with passenger counts in the bottom 25% OR cargo weights in the top 20%, what is the difference between the maximum cargo weight among remaining domestic flights and the minimum passenger count among remaining international flights that also have Boeing aircraft types and on-time performance of 'No'?

title: Railway Ticket Purchase Records
questions: Among passengers who booked through digital channels (Online or Mobile_App) and are loyalty members, but excluding those with Economy tickets traveling less than 400km, what is the average base price for passengers whose journey distance exceeds the median distance of all Business class passengers who are not loyalty members?

For passengers who either booked First_Class tickets OR have journey distances above 500km (but not both conditions simultaneously), and considering only those who are loyalty members booking through non-Station channels, what is the total base price of passengers whose ticket type differs from the most common ticket type among non-loyalty members who booked via Phone?

Among passengers whose base price per kilometer is below the average rate of Economy class loyalty members, but excluding those who booked through the same channel as the passenger with the highest total base price in Business class, what is the count of passengers whose journey distance falls within the interquartile range of all First_Class passengers who are not loyalty members?

title: Railway Ticket Purchases and Seat Assignments
questions: Among passengers who booked Economy or Business class tickets (but not First class) on routes that either start from NYC or end in NYC (but not both), and whose loyalty points are above the average loyalty points of all Business class passengers, what is the total ticket price revenue generated from passengers whose booking dates fall in the second half of January 2024?

For passengers traveling on routes where the ticket price is above the median price of all Economy class tickets, but who themselves did not book Economy class, and whose loyalty points are either below 300 or above 600 (but not between 300-600 inclusive), what is the average loyalty points of those whose passenger IDs contain an odd number when converted to numeric form (considering only the numeric part)?

Among routes that appear exactly twice in the booking records, considering only passengers whose loyalty points exceed the average of passengers on the same route, and whose seat class is not the most expensive class available on that specific route, how many passengers booked their tickets in the last 5 days of January 2024 and have ticket prices that are multiples of 25?

title: Railway Ticket Bookings with Seat Assignments
questions: Among passengers who received discounts and are traveling during peak hours, but excluding those with middle seats, what is the average cancellation fee for tickets where the passenger age is either under 30 or over 50, and the travel class is not Economy?

For routes that have both NYC-Boston and Boston-NYC bookings, considering only tickets booked after January 25th with window seats, what is the total price difference between discounted First class tickets traveling during non-peak hours versus non-discounted Business class tickets traveling during peak hours?

Among passengers aged 35-55 who booked tickets for February travel dates, excluding Economy class and middle seat assignments, how many tickets have a cancellation fee that exceeds the average cancellation fee of all discounted tickets, but only if the booking was made during peak travel periods and the route involves either Chicago or LA?

title: Real-time Traffic Condition Data
questions: Among routes with high congestion that have weather impact, calculate the average incident count for those with peak hour speeds below 42 km/h, then identify how many medium congestion routes without weather impact have incident counts greater than this calculated average?

For routes where the speed difference between off-peak and peak hours exceeds 20 km/h, filter those with either high congestion OR more than 10 incidents (but not both conditions simultaneously), then determine the total incident count for routes in this filtered set that also have weather impact?

Consider routes with low congestion levels that have no weather impact and incident counts below 3. Calculate their average off-peak speed, then count how many high congestion routes with weather impact have peak hour speeds within 5 km/h of this calculated average?

title: Real-time Traffic Condition Data
questions: Among routes with high congestion that are either incident-prone with peak volume exceeding 3000 OR non-incident-prone with average speed below 25 MPH, what is the total off-peak volume for routes where the peak-to-off-peak ratio is greater than 2.0?

For routes classified as medium congestion, calculate the average speed difference between incident-prone routes with peak volume above 2000 and non-incident-prone routes with off-peak volume below 900, then determine how many routes fall into the faster category?

Considering only routes where the combined peak and off-peak volume exceeds 4000 OR the route has low congestion with incident-prone status, what is the weighted average speed (weighted by peak volume) for routes that simultaneously have above-median off-peak volume within this filtered subset?

title: Real-time Traffic Condition Data
questions: Among routes with either severe congestion OR incidents (but not both conditions simultaneously), and where traffic volume exceeds 1500 vehicles, what is the average speed reduction percentage from normal speed for routes that have current speeds below 30 mph?

For routes where the speed efficiency ratio (current speed divided by normal speed) is less than 0.6, exclude those with light congestion, then among the remaining routes, how many have traffic volumes that exceed the median traffic volume of all routes with incidents?

Consider routes that meet exactly two of these three criteria: (1) speed reduction greater than 40%, (2) traffic volume above 1400 vehicles, (3) no incidents. Among these filtered routes, what is the difference between the highest and lowest current speeds?

title: Ride-Hailing Platform Order Data
questions: Among drivers who completed trips during peak hours with surge multipliers above 1.5 OR drivers who completed non-peak trips with ratings above 4.5, but excluding those with base fares between $15-25, what is the average trip distance for the remaining drivers?

For drivers whose total revenue (base fare × surge multiplier) exceeds $25 AND who either have ratings below 4.0 during peak hours OR ratings above 4.7 during non-peak hours, but NOT both conditions simultaneously, how many such drivers exist?

If we create a composite score calculated as (Trip_Distance × Customer_Rating × Surge_Multiplier) ÷ Base_Fare, then filter for drivers with scores above 2.5 who also meet the condition of either (peak hours AND distance > 10 miles) OR (non-peak hours AND rating > 4.4), what is the driver ID with the highest composite score?

title: Ride-hailing Platform Order Data
questions: Among orders where either surge pricing is active OR the customer is Premium (but not both conditions simultaneously), and the driver rating is above 4.0, what is the average fare amount for trips longer than 10 miles, excluding any Standard customer orders that have surge pricing active?

For orders where the driver rating is at least 4.5 AND the trip distance exceeds the median distance of all Premium customer orders, but only considering orders where surge pricing status differs from the majority surge status of that customer type, what is the total fare amount of the two highest-rated drivers?

If we rank all orders by a composite score calculated as (Driver_Rating × 2 + Trip_Distance_Miles × 0.5), then filter for orders where this score is above average AND either the fare exceeds $25 OR surge is inactive (but not both), how many Standard customer orders remain after excluding those with the lowest 25% of driver ratings?

title: Ride-hailing Platform Order Data
questions: Among orders with driver ratings above 4.0 that occurred during peak hours, but excluding those with surge multipliers above 1.5, what is the average base fare for trips longer than 10 miles, weighted by the inverse of their surge multiplier?

For orders where either the driver rating is below 4.5 OR the trip distance exceeds 12 miles (but not both conditions simultaneously), and the surge multiplier is between 1.2 and 2.0 inclusive, how many such orders have a calculated final fare (base fare × surge multiplier) that ranks in the top 30% among all orders meeting these criteria?

If we group orders by peak hours status, then within each group filter for driver ratings above the group's median rating, exclude orders with the lowest 25% of trip distances within that filtered subset, and finally apply a bonus multiplier of 1.1 to base fares for orders with surge multipliers below 1.5, what is the difference between the total adjusted revenue of peak hours orders versus non-peak hours orders?

title: Traffic Violation Penalty Records
questions: Among drivers who have accumulated more than 6 total points across all their violations, what is the average fine amount for those who have at least one unpaid violation but are not currently suspended, excluding any parking violations from the calculation?

For drivers who have both court-required violations and non-court-required violations, how many of them have a suspended license status that contradicts their payment behavior (either suspended despite paying all fines, or not suspended despite having unpaid serious violations worth more than $400)?

What is the total fine amount for violations where the driver has multiple violations, the specific violation type appears at least 3 times in the dataset, the violation requires court appearance or results in more than 4 points, and the driver's license status differs between their violations?

title: Traffic Violation Penalty Records
questions: Among violations that either require court appearance OR have unpaid status (but not both conditions simultaneously), and exclude parking violations, what is the total fine amount for violations with 3 or more points that occurred within the last 40 days?

For drivers with violations requiring court appearance, calculate the average fine amount only for those whose violations have been paid AND have point values that are either exactly 4 points OR greater than 6 points, then exclude any violation types that appear fewer than 2 times in this filtered subset.

Among speeding violations that are either unpaid with more than 3 points OR paid with court requirement (but not violations meeting both criteria), what is the count of violations where the fine amount exceeds the average fine of all non-parking violations in the dataset by at least 10%?

title: Traffic Violation Penalty Records
questions: What is the total fine amount for drivers who have unpaid violations, require court appearance, have more than 2 previous violations, but are not charged with DUI or parking violations?

Among drivers with paid violations who either have zero previous violations or have committed speeding violations with fines above $150, what is the average number of points deducted for those who don't require court appearance?

How many drivers have violations that meet all of the following criteria: either (unpaid status AND court required) or (paid status AND points deducted greater than 3), but exclude those with parking violations, and only count drivers whose previous violation count is either exactly 1 or greater than 4?
